cmp:0n6t52p0k48g97.why: The two divine names come in the basmala and again right after the praise in al-Fatiha. The repeat is worth pondering: mercy frames lordship from both sides.
cmp:0n6t52p0k48g97.relation: Mercy is named before and after the Lord of the worlds, so lordship is read through mercy.

cmp:1nivdrt11r000f.why: Five surahs open with the same praise and part right after it (Lord of the worlds, who created, who sent down, to whom belongs, originator). A classic place for memorizers to mix up surah openings.
cmp:1nivdrt11r000f.relation: Each opening praises God for a different work: lordship, creation, revelation, ownership, origination.

1:2|45:36.why: Al-Jathiya closes with the praise that opens al-Fatiha, spelling out the Lord of the worlds as Lord of the heavens and the earth. A small but real echo for pondering; a memorizer may also slip from one to the other.
1:2|45:36.relation: The brief praise of al-Fatiha is unfolded at the end of al-Jathiya.

cmp:1onz5230jajd2p.why: God as King or Owner in three settings: of the Day of Judgement, of all dominion, of people. Good for pondering the scope of His kingship, and the book discusses the two forms of the word.
cmp:1onz5230jajd2p.relation: His kingship over the Day, over all rule, and over mankind.

cmp:014drdf04bsrdf.why: A single ayah. The book remarks on the repeated pronoun inside 1:5, but there is no second place to compare, so as a card it shows nothing.

cmp:0calfu80rl1ytg.why: The path asked for in 1:6 is defined in 1:7 by repeating the word. Worth pondering: the straight path is not abstract but the path of a people God favoured.
cmp:0calfu80rl1ytg.relation: The request for the straight path is answered by naming whose path it is.

cmp:12w2hdc1sngny4.why: A single ayah (1:7). The book's note concerns the repetition of the word path across 1:6 and 1:7, which another card already shows; alone it compares nothing.

cmp:1sx25ql1mvxezp.why: Which surahs open with the bare three letters and which add a fourth letter or continue the ayah. Essential for memorizers, since these openings are easy to confuse.

cmp:0yxvz0w0sv5thy.why: The Book is guidance for the God-fearing (2:2) and the earlier scriptures guidance for people (3:4). The different addressees of guidance are worth pondering.
cmp:0yxvz0w0sv5thy.relation: Guidance offered to all people, yet benefiting only those who fear God.

2:6|36:10.why: Same sentence on the disbelievers whom warning does not move, in two surahs; 2:6 opens with a particle, 36:10 with a conjunction. A clear memorizer pair.

cmp:1c5i7yg1wmmu06.why: The hypocrites claim belief in God and the Last Day (2:8), while others are described as not believing in God nor the Last Day (4:38, 9:29). Memorizers must keep the added negation apart; the claim and the denial are worth pondering together.
cmp:1c5i7yg1wmmu06.relation: A false claim of faith beside open lack of faith, in the same words.

cmp:11za7m90ds08jb.why: Three ayat in one passage on the hypocrites end with not perceiving or not knowing. The book explains why each ending fits: deceiving and corruption are not perceived, while calling believers fools is a failure of knowledge. Useful for memorizers and for pondering.

cmp:05ikwqs1gj5l9q.why: Same triple description of the deaf, dumb and blind, ending differently in one surah: they will not return (the hypocrites) and they do not understand (the disbelievers likened to herded animals). Classic memorizer pair.
cmp:05ikwqs1gj5l9q.relation: Two kinds of blindness: those who will not come back and those who cannot understand.

cmp:0suy0jw0p4dd3m.why: A single ayah (2:21), the first call to all mankind. Nothing to compare inside the card.

cmp:0muwxke1lpa0se.why: The challenge to produce a surah (2:23, 10:38) or ten surahs (11:13), with small differences in wording. A key memorizer set and a stage-by-stage challenge worth pondering.
cmp:0muwxke1lpa0se.relation: The same challenge to bring a surah like it, phrased for different audiences.

cmp:0loqpqf156l3cx.why: The same announcement to the angels opens the story of Adam three times: a vicegerent (2:30) and a human from clay (15:28, 38:71). Same story; memorizers must track the wording.
cmp:0loqpqf156l3cx.relation: One event told with a different focus: Adam's role in 2:30, his substance in 15 and 38.

cmp:18owk8f1inraz1.why: Iblis's refusal told seven times, each with a different continuation (refused, was not among those who prostrate, said, was of the jinn, was arrogant). A central memorizer set and one story worth reading together.

cmp:1kmmyzz0z4fxkf.why: Two commands to descend within two ayat: the first states enmity and a stay on earth, the second promises guidance. The book asks why the command is repeated; good for pondering.
cmp:1kmmyzz0z4fxkf.relation: The descent comes first as consequence, then as the start of a life under guidance.

cmp:04vslnt0wo5ml1.why: The command to descend in al-Baqara, al-A'raf and Ta-Ha, with different wording (plural or dual, enmity or guidance). Same story; a strong memorizer set.

2:45|2:153.why: Same command to seek help through patience and prayer, first to the Children of Israel, then to the believers, with different endings. A memorizer pair and a link worth pondering.
2:45|2:153.relation: The command once given to Israel is given again to the believers.

cmp:0gbn0390li6xnd.why: Deliverance from Pharaoh's people told three times with small changes (slaughter or kill, saved or rescued, spoken by God or by Moses). Same story; a core memorizer set.

cmp:0fcdg8m146mf2w.why: Same closing clause: God did not wrong them but they wronged themselves. Two places are the same story of manna and quails; the third applies it to those whose spending is ruined. Good for memorizers and for pondering self-wrong.
cmp:0fcdg8m146mf2w.relation: Whatever the setting, the harm is traced back to the people themselves.

2:58|7:161.why: The command to enter the town in al-Baqara and al-A'raf, with many small swaps (enter or dwell, eat with or without the conjunction, the order of prostrating and saying the word). One of the richest memorizer pairs.

cmp:1fbst8q080b7uq.why: The same story with its sequel: the command to enter the town and the wrongdoers changing the word. The sequel also differs (sent down or sent, transgressing or wronging), so the two ayat together are needed for memorizers.

cmp:1wem4xy0kk9d0c.why: The reason for humiliation and wrath given three times: disbelief in God's signs and killing prophets. The small swaps (prophets in two plurals, without right with or without the article, the added killing of those who command justice) are classic memorizer traps.
cmp:1wem4xy0kk9d0c.relation: The same charge sheet against those who killed the prophets, in al-Baqara and Al Imran.

cmp:175r0kv0c88p3h.why: Extends the same charge to 4:155, where the verbs become nouns (their disbelief, their killing). Good for memorizers to see the verbal and noun forms side by side.

cmp:1w6kqlo055zoym.why: The list of believers, Jews, Christians and Sabians in three surahs, with the order and case of the Sabians changing and 22:17 adding Magians and polytheists with a different ending. A classic memorizer set; also worth pondering how the end differs (reward versus judgement between them).
cmp:1w6kqlo055zoym.relation: Two ayat promise reward to whoever believes; the third leaves the judgement between all groups to God.

2:63|2:93.why: The covenant and the mount raised over them, word for word, then two different continuations: remember what is in it, or hear (and they said: we hear and disobey). Memorizer pair and a telling contrast.
2:63|2:93.relation: The same covenant, recalled first as a call to remember and then as the scene of their open disobedience.

cmp:1gcfd1615lebcc.why: Their claim that the fire will touch them only for a few days, with the plural adjective in two forms. A famous memorizer pair; the books explain the difference.

cmp:096imnh1m8nsrl.why: A single ayah (2:100). There is no second place in the card to compare.

cmp:1tvufnp0hzz8jr.why: The warning not to follow their desires after knowledge has come, three times with different wording (after that which, after what, from after what) and different endings. A key memorizer set.

cmp:1ygftrd1r01aq7.why: The same warning in its two al-Baqara places, differing in the relative word and the ending. Valid pair, though it is contained in the three-ayah card on the same words.

cmp:0t11ukc0ae9o2i.why: The same statement on guidance, with its two halves inverted: God's guidance is the guidance (2:120) and the guidance is God's guidance (3:73). A sharp memorizer trap and worth pondering.
cmp:0t11ukc0ae9o2i.relation: One truth said from both ends, both answering the People of the Book.

cmp:1oo397p079cd3f.why: Abraham's prayer for the town: a town (indefinite) in 2:126, this town (definite) in 14:35, followed by different requests. Classic memorizer pair; the books link it to the town before and after it was built.
cmp:1oo397p079cd3f.relation: The same prayer, first for a place yet to become a town, then for the established town.

cmp:1fqlh380pfag7y.why: In Abraham's prayer purification comes after teaching (2:129); in the answer it comes before (3:164, 62:2). A famous memorizer point and worth pondering.
cmp:1fqlh380pfag7y.relation: The prayer and its fulfilment, with the order of purifying and teaching reversed.

cmp:1pvcnkn09ge9qv.why: The four places of the messenger who recites, purifies and teaches the Book and wisdom, with the order and pronouns changing. Core memorizer set.

2:134|2:141.why: The same refrain, word for word, closing two passages on Abraham and his sons. Memorizers need to know it occurs twice; the repeat drives home that each nation answers for its own deeds.

cmp:0nuoww51q2nzwr.why: The command to turn to the Sacred Mosque three times in one passage, each with a different continuation. The books discuss the purpose of each repeat; core memorizer set.

cmp:0bu1jda1wss6t2.why: Do not fear them, fear Me: once with the final pronoun written (2:150) and twice without it (5:3, 5:44, the latter with people named). A fine memorizer point.
cmp:0bu1jda1wss6t2.relation: The same command to fear God alone, at the qibla change, the completion of religion, and judging by the Torah.

cmp:0b65ega0qz19qa.why: The messenger sent from among you: as a favour on the believers (2:151, 3:164) and as one who cares for you (9:128). Worth pondering the closeness of the messenger to his people.
cmp:0b65ega0qz19qa.relation: The messenger from among themselves, described by his mission and by his care for them.

cmp:18bdjwz1xn6aoj.why: Those who conceal what God sent down and those who sell His covenant for a small price, with different punishments (cursed, eating fire, no share in the Hereafter). Same theme; memorizers must keep the endings apart.
cmp:18bdjwz1xn6aoj.relation: Concealing the truth and selling it cheaply, and how each is punished.

cmp:1kb727v04cpjon.why: The exception for those who repent and amend: with 'and made clear' in 2:160, with 'after that' in 3:89 and 24:5. A memorizer set; the added clarifying fits those who had concealed.
cmp:1kb727v04cpjon.relation: Repentance fitted to the sin: those who concealed must also make clear.

cmp:1xv3c6m083nzj0.why: Signs for people who use reason, in four places, each listing different signs. Memorizers need to know which closing goes with which ayah; the set invites pondering what reason should draw from creation.

cmp:0bezcjt1c9xgdz.why: God reviving the earth after its death, six times, with or without the extra particle and with different endings (resurrection, signs, most do not reason). Worth pondering as a proof of resurrection and useful for memorizers.
cmp:0bezcjt1c9xgdz.relation: The reviving of dead earth used again and again as the sign of the dead being raised.

cmp:1sezamr0zeqgql.why: The three places where rain revives the earth with the past verb, one adding the particle before 'after its death'. A fine memorizer distinction the books explain.

cmp:0qsueth1xztcub.why: Blind following of forefathers, three times, with found or met, do not reason or do not know, and Satan in the third. Classic memorizer set and the same theme.
cmp:0qsueth1xztcub.relation: The same excuse of the forefathers, answered each time by exposing what the forefathers were.

cmp:0lh789l0asllbh.why: The exception for one forced by necessity, with the endings changing (no sin on him; your Lord is forgiving; God is forgiving). Same ruling, core memorizer set.

cmp:176g62404i8w8g.why: What is dedicated to other than God: the word order of 'to it' and 'to other than God' flips between 2:173 and the other places. A famous memorizer trap explained by all three books.

cmp:1jrj90s0atifam.why: Two neighbouring ayat on bequests, parallel in form, closing with different names of God: hearing and knowing for one who alters a will, forgiving and merciful for one who sets it right. Worth pondering how each ending fits.
cmp:1jrj90s0atifam.relation: The one who corrupts a will is told God hears and knows; the one who mends it is told God forgives.

cmp:0wtnx0f1l7xbcb.why: The concession for the sick appears three times: with 'among you' in 2:184 and 2:196, without it in 2:185, and in 2:196 for the pilgrim with a ransom instead of later days. Close neighbours that memorizers mix up.

cmp:12rftp3127rxhl.why: These are God's limits: do not come near them (fasting and seclusion) and do not overstep them (divorce). Classic memorizer pair; the books explain why each verb fits.
cmp:12rftp3127rxhl.relation: Limits around desire are not to be approached; limits of rights are not to be crossed.

cmp:1a5vj8f1tgmvt5.why: Of the many 'they ask you about' ayat, only 20:105 answers with the extra particle before 'say'. The book explains it; useful for memorizers.

cmp:1k6arc21mtow84.why: The book groups three classic pairs from al-Baqara, Al Imran, al-Anfal and al-Hashr: fight them until there is no persecution (with 'all of it' in 8:39), victory only from God (word order of 'hearts' and 'by it'), and opposing God and His messenger (doubled letters and the messenger omitted in 59:4). Each pair is a strong memorizer trap, though the three pairs are different topics.

cmp:1qypawl1xw3htn.why: Did you think you would enter Paradise (or be left alone) before trials and before God makes known those who strive? Three places with different continuations; a classic memorizer set and the same theme of testing.
cmp:1qypawl1xw3htn.relation: Paradise and acceptance are not reached without being tested.

cmp:03jy1gb0z4v44j.why: Two ayat in al-Baqara end with the same closing, that God makes the signs clear so you may reflect. Memorizers must know which rulings and parables carry this ending.

cmp:0n9wasq0sizmq2.why: A single ayah (2:221). The book comments on the repeated prohibition inside it, but there is no second place to compare.

cmp:1fp9u0h1lobxph.why: Keeping in kindness or releasing in goodness (2:229) versus releasing in kindness (2:231). A small swap that memorizers trip on.

cmp:0nrmo3s15ich3y.why: When the waiting term ends: keep them in kindness or release them (2:231) or part from them (65:2). Same ruling; a classic memorizer pair.

cmp:03300io0bhub28.why: A single ayah (2:231). Nothing in the card to compare it with.

2:232|65:2.why: The same reminder closes divorce rulings in two surahs, with and without 'among you' and with 'that' in two forms. Memorizer pair on the same subject.

cmp:1fwii7w1w5l8b0.why: God is full of bounty to people but most are ungrateful: five places, ending 'most people' or 'most of them'. Memorizers need the split; the refrain invites pondering ingratitude.
cmp:1fwii7w1w5l8b0.relation: God's bounty is constant; human thanks is the exception.

cmp:10eu2ho06bivz6.why: A single ayah (2:253). The book's note is internal to it; nothing to compare.

cmp:1axysim1lxjei4.why: Seven ears of grain in two places with two plural forms (2:261 and 12:43). The book explains the choice of plural; a neat point for memorizers and for pondering abundance against scarcity.
cmp:1axysim1lxjei4.relation: Seven ears multiplying charity, and seven ears in the king's dream of plenty and drought.

cmp:02pipdg1hxxc8a.why: They have no power over anything they earned, with the two halves reversed in 14:18. Two parables of wasted deeds; a classic memorizer pair.
cmp:02pipdg1hxxc8a.relation: Charity spoiled by showing off and the deeds of disbelievers both end as nothing in hand.

cmp:1p2lvp70u9x6uf.why: A single ayah (2:271). Nothing in the card to compare.

cmp:1krzppu087ijag.why: God does not love a certain kind: the sinful disbeliever, the boastful, the treacherous. Both boastful ayat run on to those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess, which shows the link between pride and avarice. Useful for memorizers (every versus whoever was) and for pondering.
cmp:1krzppu087ijag.relation: Pride and stinginess named together twice: the boaster is the one who withholds.

cmp:1qrbyjk0xiewym.why: The same set without the run-ons: God does not love every sinful disbeliever, whoever is boastful, whoever is treacherous. The wording (every versus whoever was) shifts and memorizers mix the endings.

cmp:1tnh65913hm10h.why: He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, five times, reversed in 5:40 and with different endings. A classic memorizer set; the order invites pondering where mercy is put first and why.
cmp:1tnh65913hm10h.relation: Forgiveness comes first except in 5:40, which follows the punishment of thieves.

cmp:1ql19r90hk77p3.why: Revealing the Book with the intensive verb (3:3) and the plain one (18:1). The book discusses the two verb forms; a small point useful to memorizers.

cmp:09rrlzr1jxrflt.why: Within two ayat the Quran is sent down with one verb form and the Torah, Gospel and Criterion with another. The book explains the difference (gradual versus all at once); worth pondering.
cmp:09rrlzr1jxrflt.relation: The Quran came down in stages, the earlier scriptures at once.

cmp:0yeroni0rcnm1c.why: Only the name of the Torah is shared; 3:3 lists the scriptures sent down and 3:93 is about food made lawful before the Torah. Different subjects, nothing for a memorizer to confuse.

cmp:0zfglar1qys38v.why: Places where the earth is named before the heaven, against the usual order. The book explains why; memorizers need to know these exceptions.
cmp:0zfglar1qys38v.relation: Earth comes first where the speech is about people on earth.

cmp:0btskml170kbe5.why: God does not break His promise: spoken of Him in 3:9, spoken to Him in 3:194. A classic memorizer pair within one surah.
cmp:0btskml170kbe5.relation: The same truth, first as a statement, then as a direct plea.

cmp:1989vmk12rpwak.why: Neither wealth nor children will avail the disbelievers, three times, ending as fuel of the fire or as companions of the fire forever, with and without the opening and the conjunction. Classic memorizer set.

cmp:0lq78tb1jnqfir.why: Like the way of Pharaoh's people: denied Our signs, disbelieved in God's signs, denied their Lord's signs, then seized or destroyed. Two of these are only two ayat apart in al-Anfal. Core memorizer set and worth pondering the two stages (seizing, then drowning).
cmp:0lq78tb1jnqfir.relation: The same precedent applied twice in al-Anfal: first their disbelief and seizure, then their denial and drowning.

cmp:0wiin9j1e74ik5.why: A single ayah (3:11). The comparison is already in the three-ayah card on the same words.

cmp:1ucuxhu060at00.why: A single ayah (3:18). The book remarks on the testimony repeated inside it; there is no second place to compare.

cmp:0n1at260a0xun0.why: Submitting one's face to God, with two prepositions: to God in 3:20 and towards God in 31:22. A fine memorizer point the book explains.

cmp:0g8svw608ps07i.why: He brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, four times, with a noun instead of a verb in 6:95 and different surroundings. Core memorizer set and a sign worth pondering.
cmp:0g8svw608ps07i.relation: Life from death and death from life, used as a proof of God's sole power.

cmp:1odzayb0lgys9z.why: God warns you of Himself twice within three ayat: first closing with the return to God, then with His kindness to servants. Memorizer pair and worth pondering: the warning is itself a mercy.
cmp:1odzayb0lgys9z.relation: The same warning ends once with the return to God and once with His compassion.

cmp:153woeb0mjt9c5.why: Jesus's call to worship God his Lord and theirs, three times, with or without the conjunction and the pronoun of emphasis. Same speaker and message; a classic memorizer set.

cmp:0vznhez13e9kpr.why: The disciples' answer, 'bear witness that we are Muslims', with two forms of the pronoun in 3:52 and 5:111. Same story; a fine memorizer trap.

cmp:0rowcvh1erma9v.why: Disbelieving after their faith (3:86) and after their Islam (9:74). The book explains why: the first had borne witness to the truth, the hypocrites only outwardly submitted. Worth pondering and a memorizer trap.
cmp:0rowcvh1erma9v.relation: Apostasy after real faith versus hypocrites who had only professed Islam.

cmp:0s5ztsw1sjryle.why: Turning people away from God's path and seeking crookedness in it: said to the People of the Book (3:99) and by Shu'ayb to his people (7:86), with small wording changes. Memorizer pair and a shared theme.
cmp:0s5ztsw1sjryle.relation: The same obstruction of believers, in Madinah and in Midian.

cmp:1n9n5vr0s6jqh9.why: God did not wrong them but they wronged themselves, with and without 'were' (3:117, 16:33). A classic memorizer pair the book explains.

cmp:1ijnhy41oezpmo.why: Ranks with God: degree in the singular and degrees in the plural in neighbouring ayat (4:95, 4:96), and ranks in other surahs. The book explains the singular and plural; worth pondering how ranks follow deeds.
cmp:1ijnhy41oezpmo.relation: People are ranked by what they did: one degree over those who stayed behind, and many degrees of reward.

cmp:010pzxc1n1gjlw.why: Saying what is not in their hearts: with their mouths (3:167) and with their tongues (48:11). Two hypocrite groups, a classic memorizer pair.
cmp:010pzxc1n1gjlw.relation: The same gap between word and heart in the hypocrites of Uhud and the Bedouins who stayed behind.

cmp:1qybkxb00jnpnz.why: That is for what your hands sent forth, and God is not unjust to servants: twice the plural (3:182, 8:51), once the dual addressed to one man (22:10). Memorizer set and a firm statement of divine justice.

cmp:12avxti079iwc2.why: Patience as a matter of resolve, three times with three openings (indeed that is, then indeed that is, indeed that is surely). The book explains the added emphasis; good for memorizers and for pondering patience.
cmp:12avxti079iwc2.relation: Patience under harm from others, under trials, and in forgiving: each is called true resolve.

cmp:13dzhd00d2h6ws.why: Their refuge is Hell: an evil resting place (3:197) versus an evil destination (9:73, 66:9, which are identical). Memorizers must know the identical pair and the odd one.

cmp:0va2u5p0e1b4pl.why: Created you from one soul, then its mate: created, made, then made. Same subject, a classic memorizer set the book explains.

cmp:1fvxhpa0wzn6s8.why: He who created you: from one soul, from clay, produced you from one soul. Same subject of human origin with different verbs and continuations; useful for memorizers.
cmp:1fvxhpa0wzn6s8.relation: Human origin traced to one soul and to clay, each followed by a different lesson.

4:5|4:8.why: Provide for them and speak to them kindly: to the weak-minded and to relatives at the division of inheritance. Same command in neighbouring ayat; worth pondering that giving is paired with kind words.
4:5|4:8.relation: Material help always joined to kind speech.

cmp:07iuo660x7nt3o.why: A single ayah (4:12). The book's note is on the repeated phrases inside it; nothing to compare.

cmp:03loa2b0qcudf3.why: Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding there: with or without 'forever', with or without the preposition before 'beneath' (9:100). These small additions are classic memorizer traps, even though the promise is a common formula.

4:13|9:89.why: The same reward and ending, with and without the conjunction before 'that is the great success'. A tight memorizer pair.

cmp:19hsvdr0jjays7.why: Fifteen places of the gardens formula with different subjects and endings. As one card it is too wide to learn from; the real traps are already in the smaller cards on the same promise. Two rows of 61:10 to 61:12 do not carry the phrase themselves.

cmp:1d21wc01jofgya.why: The same opening describes two opposite spenders: those who spend for God without reminders or harm (2:262, 2:274) and those who spend to be seen and do not believe (4:38). One promised reward with no fear, the other given Satan as a companion.
cmp:1d21wc01jofgya.relation: Contrast: sincere spending and spending for show, opened with the same words, end in opposite fates.

cmp:0tbk8g5027x5rn.why: Both describe the one who spends to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the Last Day. A memorizer must keep the singular form with one negation (2:264) apart from the plural form with a repeated negation (4:38).
cmp:0tbk8g5027x5rn.relation: Same theme: showing off ruins charity; 2:264 gives the parable of the bare rock, 4:38 names Satan as the companion.

cmp:1yfojvt1sz9t4d.why: The same promise of full recompense on the Day, each soul paid what it earned without wrong, closes three ayat. The memorizer must separate the two openings of the clause (2:281 and 3:161 against 3:25).
cmp:1yfojvt1sz9t4d.relation: Same theme: full and just recompense, in the context of the final return (2:281), the gathering (3:25) and the one who defrauds (3:161).

cmp:0bg07hf1kbmkz5.why: Many places of God's ownership of the heavens and the earth with different tails, a real memorizer set. But in the four glorification openings (59:1, 61:1, 62:1, 64:1) the same words have a different structure: what is in the heavens glorifies God, it is not a statement of what belongs to Him.
cmp:0bg07hf1kbmkz5.changes: Split into the ownership statements and the glorification openings, since the shared words are a different phrase structure in the second group. Run-on rows kept as they were.
cmp:0bg07hf1kbmkz5.relation: God owns all that is in the heavens and the earth, and each place draws a different consequence: reckoning, the return of all matters, forgiveness, encompassing knowledge, self-sufficiency, sufficiency as guardian, just recompense.

cmp:18thk590qsrikf.why: He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, each time tied to His dominion over the heavens and the earth, with four different endings to keep apart. Even the claim of the Jews and Christians (5:18) is answered with the same rule.
cmp:18thk590qsrikf.relation: Same theme: forgiveness and punishment rest on God's will and ownership, not on lineage or claims.

cmp:1uy93c51vi1uyf.why: Only the stock closing that God is able to do all things after a verb of willing is shared. The subjects differ (reckoning of hidden thoughts, the divinity of the Messiah, punishment and forgiveness, spoils given without fighting), and the rows run on into unrelated ayat.

2:284|59:6.why: Shared only a stock closing about God's will and His power over all things. One ayah is about the reckoning of what is in the soul, the other about spoils taken without battle; nothing to ponder together.

cmp:1d601c203ofhpy.why: The Book sent down with the truth, confirming what came before it, in two places that differ in their opening verb and preposition and in what follows (the Torah and Gospel, or guardianship over earlier scripture). A clear memorizer pair.
cmp:1d601c203ofhpy.relation: Same theme: the Quran confirms the earlier scriptures; 5:48 adds that it stands guard over them.

cmp:0pcyr5f1h6le5r.why: The only two places that close with this declaration of oneness joined to the Mighty and the Wise, both in the opening of Al Imran, so a memorizer can mix them. One follows the shaping in the womb, the other the testimony of God, the angels and the people of knowledge.

cmp:087c0ij1lh0jn5.why: Only a short opening is shared, and what is sent down differs in each place: the Book, rain, tranquillity. A stock opening with three different subjects; not a mutashabih and too thin for pondering.

3:10|3:116.why: The same sentence that wealth and children will not help the deniers against God, in two places of one surah, ending differently: fuel of the Fire in one, companions of the Fire abiding forever in the other. A classic memorizer pair.

3:11|8:52.why: These two ayat are already in the fuller card of the same phrase (3:11, 8:52, 8:54), which shows the third variant too. This pair adds nothing beyond it.

cmp:11vc3bc0dr9s42.why: Two messages ordered to the deniers, both tied to Badr: one warns they will be overcome and gathered to Hell, the other offers forgiveness of the past if they stop. The short shared command frames threat and invitation side by side.
cmp:11vc3bc0dr9s42.relation: Contrast: the warning of defeat and the open door of forgiveness, both addressed to the same deniers.

cmp:0hajxa31spsasn.why: The exact closing that this is a lesson for those with insight occurs only here: after the two armies at Badr and after the alternation of night and day. A memorizer needs it, and it shows that history and nature are both read as signs.
cmp:0hajxa31spsasn.relation: Similarity: an event of history and a daily sight of nature are both called a lesson for those who see.

cmp:1fu4xqk1vg3lio.why: The promise of gardens with rivers flowing beneath, abiding there, recurs with a different tail each time (the great triumph, the reward of the doers of good, an excellent reward for the workers, forever, pleased with them). The tails are exactly what a memorizer confuses, and the books treat this set as a mutashabih.
cmp:1fu4xqk1vg3lio.relation: Same promise given to many kinds of people: the God-fearing, the obedient, the truthful, those who believe and do good, those who love none of God's enemies.

cmp:1qk8bgx06f7gh5.why: A near copy of the fuller card of the same promise (the gardens with rivers flowing beneath, abiding), only missing the three places with the gardens of Eden and the lofty chambers. It adds nothing that the fuller card does not show.

cmp:1snhr9x0kvu3th.why: The supplications of the righteous, each introduced the same way: forgive us and protect us from the Fire (3:16), turn away the punishment of Hell (25:65), grant us comfort in our spouses and children (25:74). Useful for the memorizer and a short lesson in what the believers ask for.
cmp:1snhr9x0kvu3th.relation: Same theme: the prayers that mark the God-fearing and the servants of the Merciful.

cmp:0el53tg1j6h0g4.why: Three places say the earlier communities split only after knowledge reached them, out of rivalry among themselves. The verbs and what follows differ, which is the memorizer's task, and the lesson is the same: division came from envy, not from ignorance.
cmp:0el53tg1j6h0g4.relation: Same theme: religious division born of rivalry after clear knowledge.

cmp:0j380y40v3hoe0.why: The people of the Book divided only after the proof came to them, said twice with different words for the dividing and for what came (knowledge, the clear proof). A memorizer pair with one lesson.
cmp:0j380y40v3hoe0.relation: Same theme: the people of the Book differed after the truth was made clear to them.

cmp:0qmlek415okxxy.why: Only the common opening about those who disbelieve is shared. One describes killing the prophets and those who command justice, the other separating God from His messengers and believing in part. Different charges, a stock opening, nothing to set side by side.

3:22|3:56.why: The same closing that the deniers have no helpers in this world or the next, after their deeds are made void (3:22) and after they are punished severely (3:56). A memorizer pair in one surah with one lesson: nothing saves them in either life.
3:22|3:56.relation: Same theme: the loss of the deniers in both worlds, once in their deeds and once in their punishment.

cmp:0ylmag41fdj2cw.why: The same address about those given a portion of the Book, three times, each naming another fault: turning away from God's judgment, buying error, believing in idols and false gods. A clear memorizer set and a portrait of one group.
cmp:0ylmag41fdj2cw.relation: Same subject: three faults of those who were given a share of the scripture.

cmp:15uftyl12a4eot.why: Only a short causal opening is shared. One gives the reason for the Jews' false security about the Fire, the other the hypocrites' promise to obey the haters of revelation. Different subjects and nothing to learn together.

cmp:1mz318p1ly29y5.why: God knows what is in the heavens and the earth, four times with different frames and endings (all-powerful, all-knowing, the secret councils). A memorizer set, and each place applies the same knowledge to something hidden: what is in breasts, one's religion, private talk.
cmp:1mz318p1ly29y5.relation: Same theme: nothing is hidden from God, applied to hearts, claims of faith and secret talk.

3:29|49:16.why: Both ayat are already in the fuller card of the same phrase (3:29, 5:97, 49:16, 58:7), which shows their different endings with the others. The pair adds nothing.

3:29|3:189.why: Only the stock closing about God's power over all things is shared. One is about God knowing what is in hearts, the other about His dominion over the heavens and the earth; the rows run on into unrelated ayat.

cmp:0c2yh5k09bjrje.why: A question of where something came from gets two opposite answers. Mary says her provision is from God; after Uhud the believers are told their disaster is from themselves. The same question and answer frame makes the contrast stand out.
cmp:0c2yh5k09bjrje.relation: Contrast: blessing is traced to God, the defeat to the believers' own doing.

cmp:0wlehk11kjkg89.why: Two addresses of the angels to Mary three ayat apart, one with the conjunction and one without, the first about her being chosen and purified, the second the good news of Jesus. A memorizer must keep the openings and messages in order.
cmp:0wlehk11kjkg89.relation: Same story: the two announcements of the angels to Mary.

cmp:1v2fsft17dm3rj.why: Story closings that call the story news of the unseen revealed to the Prophet, who was not present (Mary in 3:44, Joseph in 12:102), and news of the towns narrated (11:100). The two unseen closings are near identical and must be told apart.
cmp:1v2fsft17dm3rj.relation: Same theme: the stories are proof of revelation, since the Prophet did not witness them.

cmp:0w14ctw0o1f4js.why: Jesus says he confirms the Torah before him, then in one place permits some of what was forbidden and in the other gives the good news of a messenger named Ahmad. A memorizer pair with a clear thread.
cmp:0w14ctw0o1f4js.relation: Same speaker and claim: Jesus confirms what came before him and points to what comes after.

cmp:15jjtaf111oncb.why: Jesus' call for helpers and the disciples' answer, told as the event in 3:52 and given to the believers as a model in 61:14. The shared exchange is long and exact; what follows differs.
cmp:15jjtaf111oncb.relation: Same story: the disciples answering Jesus, then held up as the example the believers should follow.

cmp:01ybi3u1ul3ivk.why: Three times God addresses Jesus by name: the promise to take him up and purify him, the reminder of favours, and the question on the Day whether he told people to worship him and his mother. The openings differ in the conjunction and in adding his mother's name, which is the memorizer's point.
cmp:01ybi3u1ul3ivk.relation: Same person: God's three addresses to Jesus, from his raising to the questioning on the Day.

cmp:1t8w6tt018lgyd.why: The fate of the deniers in three places where a passage sets the two groups against each other, each with a different continuation: punishment in both worlds, brought into the punishment, rebuked for their arrogance. The opening conjunction also differs, a known memorizer trap.
cmp:1t8w6tt018lgyd.relation: Same theme: the deniers' end, each time the second half of a contrast with the believers.

cmp:0t4l6k21hr9ep8.why: The believers' reward stated six times in the same frame, with different conjunctions and different rewards (full wages, mercy and grace, a garden where they rejoice, gardens of refuge, mercy as the clear triumph). The memorizer needs the tree, and each place is half of a contrast with the deniers.
cmp:0t4l6k21hr9ep8.relation: Same theme: the reward of those who believe and do good, set against the deniers in each passage.

cmp:1huderv0m8ezrr.why: Short emphatic verdicts that open alike: this is the true story, this is the great triumph, this is the clear trial, this is certain truth. A memorizer can mix the short ones, but the subjects differ and the link rests only on the opening.

cmp:09ygkyj1at9hxd.why: The command to address the people of the Book, six times, each with a different question or call: a common word, why do you deny, why do you bar the way, do you resent us, you stand on nothing, do not exceed bounds. One addressee and a set the memorizer must order.
cmp:09ygkyj1at9hxd.relation: Same addressee: the Prophet's calls and rebukes to the people of the Book.

cmp:1qigl1z02qygfj.why: Three rebukes in one passage, each asking the people of the Book why: why argue about Abraham, why deny God's signs while you witness, why mix truth with falsehood. Close together and alike, a clear memorizer set.
cmp:1qigl1z02qygfj.relation: Same addressee: three charges against the people of the Book in one passage.

cmp:0ahewlq1i9f7dg.why: A party wished to lead the believers (3:69) or the Prophet (4:113) astray, and the answer is the same: they mislead only themselves. The tails differ (they do not perceive, they cannot harm you).
cmp:0ahewlq1i9f7dg.relation: Same theme: the plot to mislead turns back on those who plot.

3:70|3:98.why: The same question why you deny God's signs, once with a direct address and the ending that they witness it, once with the command to say it and the ending that God witnesses what they do. A sharp memorizer pair.
3:70|3:98.relation: Similarity: they witness the truth, and God witnesses their deeds.

cmp:0o07j9m1xew0u2.why: Bounty is in God's hand, He gives it to whom He wills, said in two answers to the people of the Book, with two endings (All-Encompassing and Knowing, or Possessor of great bounty). A classic memorizer pair on one theme.
cmp:0o07j9m1xew0u2.relation: Same theme: the people of the Book cannot restrict God's favour to themselves.

cmp:0aty2ze00a37f2.why: Two groups of the people of the Book in one passage, those who betray trusts and those who twist the scripture, closed by the same charge that they speak lies about God knowingly. The memorizer must link each lead-in to the closing.
cmp:0aty2ze00a37f2.relation: Same theme: two kinds of deliberate lying about God by people who know.

cmp:0nmoknw1ps1ehm.why: The only two places that say what is not fitting for a human: a prophet given the Book cannot call people to worship him, and no human is spoken to by God except by revelation, from behind a veil or through a messenger. One has the conjunction, one does not. A thin but real link around the limits of a human messenger.
cmp:0nmoknw1ps1ehm.relation: Similarity: both set the limits of a human who receives revelation.

cmp:080n0wj09xpue3.why: God took a covenant twice in one surah: from the prophets, who affirmed it, and from those given the Book, who threw it behind their backs. Same words, opposite responses.
cmp:080n0wj09xpue3.relation: Contrast: the prophets kept the covenant, the people of the Book sold it for a small price.

cmp:0lazdrn02iyanb.why: The religion of Abraham, upright and not of the polytheists, in three commands to follow it, each with a different lead-in (God has spoken the truth, my Lord guided me, We revealed to you). A memorizer set with one theme.
cmp:0lazdrn02iyanb.relation: Same theme: Islam presented as the religion of Abraham.

cmp:1asq4hm0dfnfk2.why: Calls to the believers that set a condition on their own action: obey the people of the Book or the deniers and you will be turned back (3:100, 3:149); fear God or help Him and He will give criterion and victory (8:29, 47:7). But 49:6 is a different structure: the condition is a sinner bringing news, not an act of the believers.
cmp:1asq4hm0dfnfk2.changes: Removed 49:6, where the condition is a sinner's report, not the believers' act.
cmp:1asq4hm0dfnfk2.relation: Contrast: obeying others turns the believers back, obeying God brings help and forgiveness.

cmp:1wic4ou1b2z75i.why: Four warnings not to be like others: those who split after clear proofs, those who say we hear and do not hear, those who went out in pride and for show, those who forgot God. Each names a type to avoid, a useful set to ponder and to memorize.
cmp:1wic4ou1b2z75i.relation: Same theme: four negative models the believers are told not to resemble.

cmp:1541cq808tkw7c.why: Six prohibitions on taking certain people as intimate friends or allies, each naming a different group (outsiders, the deniers, Jews and Christians, mockers of the religion, fathers and brothers who prefer disbelief, God's enemies). One theme with branches a memorizer must keep apart.
cmp:1541cq808tkw7c.relation: Same theme: whom the believers must not take as allies, and why.

cmp:04otx9a12yfe7m.why: God gave victory at Badr when the believers were few and weak, and at Hunayn their large numbers did not help them. The same opening sets the two battles side by side.
cmp:04otx9a12yfe7m.relation: Contrast: victory in weakness at Badr, near defeat in self-admiration at Hunayn.

1:6|4:68.why: The prayer for the straight path, and the promise that those who obey would be guided to it: the request and its answer.
1:6|4:68.relation: Request and answer: the worshipper asks for the straight path, and 4:68 says obedience is how it is given.

1:2|6:45.why: Only the praise formula is shared; one is the opening praise, the other closes the account of the wrongdoers being cut off. Different subjects, and the phrase is too common to teach a memorizer anything.

1:6|6:87.why: The prayer for the straight path beside the prophets and their families whom Allah chose and guided to it: the reader asks for the path the prophets walked.
1:6|6:87.relation: The worshipper asks for the path; 6:87 shows who was already guided to it.

1:2|10:10.why: The phrase that opens the Quran is the last call of the people of Paradise. A known point for pondering: praise is the first and the last word.
1:2|10:10.relation: The opening praise of the Book is also the final call of the dwellers of Paradise.

1:6|10:25.why: Only the stock phrase about guiding whom He wills to a straight path; a personal prayer against a general statement about the call to the abode of peace. Too common to add anything.

1:2|14:39.why: Only the opening words of praise are shared; 14:39 is Ibrahim thanking Allah for his sons in old age. Different subjects, nothing to learn from the pairing.

1:6|16:121.why: The prayer for the straight path beside Ibrahim, who was chosen and guided to it because he was grateful: a model of the answered prayer.
1:6|16:121.relation: The path asked for in 1:6 is the path Ibrahim was guided to, and gratitude is named as the way.

1:6|24:46.why: Only the stock phrase about guiding whom He wills to a straight path; 24:46 is about the clear signs sent down. Different subjects.

1:2|35:34.why: Only the opening words of praise; 35:34 is the people of Paradise thanking Allah for removing grief. The shared words are too common to make a card.

1:2|37:182.why: Only the praise formula, here as the closing line of a surah. A memorizer will not confuse the opening of the Fatiha with this, and the subjects differ.

1:2|40:65.why: Only the praise formula closing a call to sincere worship. Stock phrase, different subjects.

1:6|67:22.why: Only the words straight path; 67:22 is a parable comparing the one walking prone with the one walking upright. The link to the prayer is thin.

2:23|2:94.why: Only the challenge formula is shared; one challenges the doubters to bring a surah, the other challenges the claim to the hereafter by wishing for death. Different subjects.

2:37|2:160.why: Adam's repentance accepted and the promise to accept those who hid the truth then repented: both end with the same divine name of accepting repentance.
2:37|2:160.relation: The first repentance in human history and the door left open for later sinners, closed with the same name.

2:39|2:81.why: Two descriptions of the people of the Fire, one by disbelief and denial, one by sin that surrounds a person, ending in the same verdict. Useful for memorizers and for pondering who earns it.
2:39|2:81.relation: Two routes, disbelief and being engulfed by one's sins, end in the same eternal Fire.

2:40|2:47.why: The same call to the Children of Israel to remember the favour, continuing two ways. A classic place for a memorizer to slip.

2:40|2:122.why: 2:122 repeats 2:47 word for word, and 2:40 with 2:47 is already a card. This pairing adds nothing that card does not show.

cmp-card:2:62|2:112,2:62|2:262,2:62|2:27.why: Four groups in one surah promised the same reward and freedom from fear and grief: the believers of all communities, the one who submits, the one who spends without reproach, the one who prays and gives zakat. Strong for memorizers and for pondering who earns it.
cmp-card:2:62|2:112,2:62|2:262,2:62|2:27.relation: Different deeds, one promised reward: no fear and no grief.

2:68|2:69.why: Consecutive questions about the cow, each asking again for a detail: same opening, different question. The story shows the people making it harder for themselves.
2:68|2:69.relation: Same story: repeated questions that only add restrictions.

2:94|2:111.why: Two claims of the People of the Book to own the hereafter or Paradise, each met with a challenge to prove it if they are truthful.
2:94|2:111.relation: Same theme: the claim to exclusive Paradise, answered by a demand for proof.

2:97|2:170.why: Only scattered common words; Jibril bringing the revelation versus following the fathers. Different subjects.

2:103|2:239.why: Only common words like believing and knowing; a reward the Jews missed versus prayer in fear. Different subjects.

2:103|2:278.why: Only the common words believe and fear Allah; different subjects (the reward missed by the sorcerers' followers, and leaving usury).

2:103|2:280.why: Only the ending about what is better if you knew; different subjects (the missed reward, and giving debtors time).

2:106|2:148.why: Only the stock closing about Allah's power over all things; abrogation versus each having a direction. Different subjects.

cmp-card:2:110|2:277,2:112|2:277.why: Prayer and zakat with the promise that good is found with Allah, then the same promise phrased as reward with their Lord and no fear or grief. Shows how one surah repeats the same reward for the same deeds.
cmp-card:2:110|2:277,2:112|2:277.relation: The deeds of 2:110 and the reward of 2:112 meet in 2:277.

2:111|2:135.why: Two claims of the Jews and Christians in the same passage, each opened with the same words and each answered by the Prophet: one asks for their proof, the other points to the way of Ibrahim.
2:111|2:135.relation: Same theme: exclusive claims to salvation and guidance, answered two ways.

cmp-card:2:112|2:262,2:112|2:274.why: Submitting to Allah and spending in His way, by day and night, earn the same reward with the same closing words. Good for a memorizer to see where each ending sits.
cmp-card:2:112|2:262,2:112|2:274.relation: Different deeds, one reward: no fear and no grief.

2:129|2:151.why: Ibrahim's prayer for a messenger and its fulfilment, in nearly the same words; in the answer, purification comes before teaching. A well-known point for pondering and a place memorizers mix up.
2:129|2:151.relation: Prayer and answer: Ibrahim asked for a messenger, and 2:151 says he was sent.

cmp-card:2:144|2:149,2:144|2:150.why: The command to face the Sacred Mosque repeated three times with different continuations. A classic spot for memorizers.
cmp-card:2:144|2:149,2:144|2:150.relation: Same command, repeated for emphasis with a new reason each time.

2:154|2:190.why: Only the phrase in the way of Allah is shared; the martyrs being alive versus the command to fight without transgressing. The phrase is stock.

2:154|2:244.why: Only the phrase in the way of Allah is shared; the martyrs being alive versus the command to fight. The phrase is stock.

2:168|2:208.why: The same warning not to follow Satan's footsteps, said first to all people about food and then to the believers about entering Islam fully. Same ending, different openings: useful for memorizers.
2:168|2:208.relation: Satan's steps are a danger in what we eat and in how fully we submit.

cmp-card:2:190|2:195,2:190|2:244.why: Fight in the way of Allah but do not transgress, for He does not love transgressors; spend in His way and do good, for He loves those who do good. A clear contrast, plus the repeated command to fight.
cmp-card:2:190|2:195,2:190|2:244.relation: Contrast in one passage: what Allah does not love and what He loves.

2:262|2:274.why: Two descriptions of those who spend, one by the absence of reproach, one by spending day and night, secretly and openly, with the same reward. Memorizers need to know which wording goes where.
2:262|2:274.relation: Two qualities of spending, one promised reward.

cmp-card:2:262|2:277,2:274|2:277.why: The spenders and the believers who pray and give zakat share the same reward line. Useful for memorizers and for seeing that spending stands beside prayer.
cmp-card:2:262|2:277,2:274|2:277.relation: Different deeds, one reward: no fear and no grief.

2:51|23:41.why: Only the word wrongdoers is shared; the calf worship versus the blast that destroyed a people. Different subjects.

2:53|23:49.why: The same statement that Musa was given the Book so people would be guided; one adds the criterion and addresses the Israelites, the other speaks of them. A memorizer's trap.
2:53|23:49.relation: Same purpose of the Book given to Musa: guidance.

2:92|23:41.why: Only the word wrongdoers is shared; the calf worship versus the blast that destroyed a people. Different subjects.

2:11|26:152.why: Corrupters in the land who do not set things right: the hypocrites claim they are reformers, and Salih's people are described as those who corrupt and do not reform.
2:11|26:152.relation: Corruption that calls itself reform, and the plain verdict on corrupters.

2:117|26:24.why: Only the words heavens and earth; creation by the word Be versus Musa answering Pharaoh about the Lord. Different subjects.

2:204|35:5.why: Only the words the life of this world are shared; the man whose speech impresses versus the warning not to be deceived. The link is thin.

2:284|35:1.why: Only heavens and earth and the stock closing about Allah's power; reckoning of hidden thoughts versus the angels as messengers. Different subjects.

2:66|36:9.why: Only the words before and behind; a punishment made an example versus a barrier set before the deniers. Different subjects.

2:66|36:45.why: Only the words before and behind; a punishment made an example versus a call to fear what is ahead. Different subjects.

2:77|36:76.why: The same statement that Allah knows what they hide and what they show, once as a rebuke to the Jews, once as comfort to the Prophet. Same words, two uses.
2:77|36:76.relation: Allah's knowledge of the hidden as a warning to some and a comfort to the Messenger.

2:131|36:58.why: Only the word Lord and a shared root; Ibrahim's submission versus the greeting of peace in Paradise. Different scenes.

2:154|37:36.why: Only the verb of saying; martyrs alive versus the idolaters calling the Prophet a mad poet. Different subjects.

2:66|41:42.why: Only the words before and behind; a punishment made an example versus falsehood not reaching the Quran. Different subjects.

2:82|41:8.why: Only the generic formula of those who believe and do good, followed by different rewards. A stock phrase; nothing specific to ponder.

2:86|41:31.why: Only the pair this world and the Hereafter; those who sold the Hereafter versus the angels' promise to the steadfast. The shared wording is stock.

2:70|43:49.why: Two peoples ask Musa to call his Lord for them and promise they will then be guided: the Israelites about the cow, Pharaoh's people under punishment. Both are evasion dressed as a request.
2:70|43:49.relation: Same request to Musa from two peoples, with the same empty promise of being guided.

2:92|43:38.why: Only scattered words; the calf after Musa versus the regret of the one with an evil companion. Different subjects.

2:117|43:9.why: Only the words heavens and earth; creation by command versus the idolaters admitting who created them. Different subjects.

2:131|43:89.why: Only a shared root of peace and submission; Ibrahim's submission versus the Prophet told to turn away. Different subjects.

2:97|46:30.why: The Quran described as confirming what came before it and guiding, once about Jibril bringing it, once by the jinn who heard it. A rare shared description.
2:97|46:30.relation: The revelation confirms earlier scripture and guides, said by Allah and repeated by the jinn.

2:98|46:6.why: Only the roots of enmity and disbelief; enmity to Allah's angels versus idols disowning their worshippers. Different subjects.

2:107|46:32.why: Only the common idea of no protector besides Allah, in a stock wording; the dominion of Allah versus the jinn warning those who ignore the caller. Different subjects.

2:176|46:2.why: Only the Book sent down from Allah; disputes about the Book versus a surah opening formula. Too common.

2:209|46:2.why: Only the names Mighty and Wise, a stock pair. Different subjects.

2:284|46:33.why: Only heavens and earth and the stock closing about Allah's power. Different subjects.

2:106|48:21.why: Only the stock closing about Allah's power over all things; abrogation versus spoils not yet won. Different subjects.

2:107|48:14.why: Only the dominion of the heavens and earth, a stock phrase; no protector versus forgiving whom He wills. Different subjects.

2:117|48:7.why: Only the words heavens and earth; creation by command versus Allah's hosts. Different subjects.

2:119|48:8.why: The Prophet's mission in the same words, a bringer of good news and a warner; 48:8 adds witness. A memorizer must know which version has what.

2:148|48:21.why: Only the stock closing about Allah's power over all things; racing to good deeds versus spoils not yet won. Different subjects.

2:209|48:7.why: Only the names Mighty and Wise, a stock closing. Different subjects.

2:209|48:19.why: Only the names Mighty and Wise, a stock closing. Different subjects.

2:284|48:14.why: The same declaration: to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and earth, He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. One closes on His power, the other on His forgiveness, which a memorizer must keep apart.
2:284|48:14.relation: Allah's ownership of all things grounds His right to forgive and to punish.

2:95|49:1.why: Only the words for what hands put forward and the name Knowing; the Jews not wishing for death versus manners before the Prophet. Different subjects.

2:103|49:1.why: Only the common words believe and fear Allah. Different subjects.

2:107|49:16.why: Only heavens and earth and a verb of knowing. Different subjects.

2:116|49:16.why: Only the stock phrase of what is in the heavens and earth. Different subjects.

2:137|49:1.why: Only the names Hearing and Knowing, a stock closing. Different subjects.

2:160|49:10.why: Only the roots of setting right and mercy; repentance versus brotherhood among believers. Different subjects.

2:182|49:10.why: Both command making peace between people: between heirs after an unjust bequest, and between believers who fight. Same act of reconciliation, closed with mercy.
2:182|49:10.relation: Reconciling people is praised in family disputes and in disputes among believers.

2:192|49:5.why: Only the stock closing Forgiving, Merciful. Different subjects.

2:224|49:1.why: Only fearing Allah and the names Hearing and Knowing. Different subjects.

2:224|49:13.why: Only the root of fearing Allah and the name Knowing. Different subjects.

2:284|49:16.why: Only the stock phrase of what is in the heavens and earth. Different subjects.

2:32|51:30.why: Angels speaking, both closing on the names Knowing and Wise, in reverse order. A clear memorizer point.
2:32|51:30.relation: The angels confess Allah's knowledge and wisdom, once about Adam, once about Ibrahim's son.

2:55|51:44.why: The same punishment, the thunderbolt that took them while they watched: the Israelites who demanded to see Allah, and Thamud who defied His command. Address versus report: you versus them.
2:55|51:44.relation: Same punishment for two peoples who rebelled against what was asked of them.

cmp-card:2:86|59:3,2:201|59:3.why: This world and the Hereafter set side by side three ways: those who sold the Hereafter, the believers asking for good in both and protection from the Fire, and a people spared punishment in this world but left with the Fire.
cmp-card:2:86|59:3,2:201|59:3.relation: Contrast: the believers ask good in both worlds and safety from the Fire; the deniers face punishment in both.

2:116|59:24.why: Only the stock phrase of what is in the heavens and earth. Different subjects.

2:148|59:6.why: Only the stock closing about Allah's power over all things. Different subjects.

2:190|60:8.why: Two rules for dealing with others: fight those who fight you and do not transgress; be kind and just to those who did not fight you. One says whom Allah does not love, the other whom He loves.
2:190|60:8.relation: Contrast in the rules of war and peace.

2:218|60:7.why: Only the stock closing Forgiving, Merciful. Different subjects.

2:101|63:1.why: Only the words a messenger of Allah came; the People of the Book casting the Book aside versus the hypocrites' false testimony. Different subjects.

2:29|65:12.why: Both speak of the creation of seven heavens and of Allah's knowledge of all things. A real shared subject.
2:29|65:12.relation: The seven heavens as a sign of Allah's knowledge and power.

2:148|65:3.why: Only the words all things. Different subjects.

2:261|65:12.why: Only the number seven. Different subjects.

2:284|65:3.why: Only the words all things. Different subjects.

2:284|65:12.why: Only heavens and earth and the stock closing about Allah's power. Different subjects.

2:173|66:1.why: Only the root of forbidding and the stock closing Forgiving, Merciful; the food laws versus the Prophet forbidding himself something. A possible point that only Allah sets what is lawful, but the wording is too thin.

2:199|66:1.why: Only the stock closing Forgiving, Merciful. Different subjects.

2:207|66:1.why: A rare phrase, seeking the pleasure of, used once for Allah and once for wives. The contrast itself is the lesson.
2:207|66:1.relation: Contrast: one sells himself seeking Allah's pleasure; the Prophet is gently asked why he sought his wives' pleasure.

2:218|66:1.why: Only the stock closing Forgiving, Merciful. Different subjects.

2:104|67:28.why: Only painful punishment for the disbelievers, a stock phrase. Different subjects.

2:88|69:41.why: The rare rebuke little do they believe, said of the Jews who claimed sealed hearts and of the Makkans who called the Quran poetry. Both refuse the revelation.
2:88|69:41.relation: Two excuses for rejecting revelation, met by the same rebuke.

2:66|72:27.why: Only the words before and behind. Different subjects.

cmp-card:2:48|82:19,2:123|82:19.why: The Day when no soul can help another: twice in al-Baqara with intercession and ransom swapped, and once in 82:19 with all command belonging to Allah. A strong memorizer pair plus a theme.
cmp-card:2:48|82:19,2:123|82:19.relation: Same Day, described as one where no soul avails another.

2:82|84:25.why: Only the generic formula of those who believe and do good; different rewards follow. Stock phrase.

cmp-card:2:25|85:11,2:82|85:11.why: Only the generic reward formula for those who believe and do good, with gardens beneath which rivers flow. It recurs across the Quran; this grouping gives nothing particular.

2:107|85:9.why: Only the dominion of the heavens and earth, a stock phrase. Different subjects.

2:116|85:9.why: Only heavens and earth. Different subjects.

2:39|90:19.why: The same verdict on those who reject Our signs: they are the people of the Fire, called in 90:19 the people of the left. Same subject, two wordings.
2:39|90:19.relation: Rejecting the signs and its end, named two ways.

2:82|95:6.why: Only the generic formula of those who believe and do good. Stock phrase; nothing particular to learn.

2:82|98:7.why: Only the generic formula of those who believe and do good. Stock phrase; nothing particular to learn.

2:209|98:4.why: Only the common phrase after the clear proofs came; slipping versus the People of the Book dividing. Different subjects.

2:82|103:3.why: Only the generic formula of those who believe and do good. Stock phrase; nothing particular to learn.

3:4|3:11.why: Those who deny Allah's signs and their severe punishment, stated generally in 3:4 and shown in Pharaoh's people in 3:11.
3:4|3:11.relation: A rule and its example: denial of the signs brings severe punishment.

3:6|3:62.why: Within Al Imran, both close on the declaration that there is no god but Him, then the names Mighty and Wise, as 3:18 does. A memorizer must place each closing.
3:6|3:62.relation: The surah keeps returning to the oneness of Allah closed with His might and wisdom.

cmp-card:3:15|3:198,3:136|3:198.why: Three places in one surah describing gardens with rivers flowing beneath, abiding, each with a different addition (spouses and good pleasure, forgiveness, hospitality from Allah). Useful for a memorizer to keep the endings apart.
cmp-card:3:15|3:198,3:136|3:198.relation: The same Garden, offered to the God-fearing and the repentant, described with different gifts.

3:18|3:62.why: Two declarations of oneness in the same surah, both closing on the names Mighty and Wise. A memorizer's point and a repeated theme.
3:18|3:62.relation: Allah's own witness to His oneness, and the true story that proves it.

3:19|3:199.why: Two kinds of People of the Book: those who differed out of envy, and those who believe humbly. Both close on Allah being swift in reckoning.
3:19|3:199.relation: Contrast within the People of the Book, both told reckoning is swift.

3:21|3:181.why: The crime of killing prophets without right, named twice, each followed by a promised punishment.
3:21|3:181.relation: Same crime of the People of the Book, recorded and answered.

3:25|3:161.why: The same line, every soul paid in full for what it earned and none wronged, about the gathering Day and about whoever cheats. A memorizer pair.
3:25|3:161.relation: Full repayment on the Day, applied to a general and a specific sin.

3:29|3:165.why: Only the stock closing about Allah's power over all things. Different subjects.

3:31|3:129.why: Only the stock closing Forgiving, Merciful. Different subjects.

3:33|3:42.why: Allah chose Al Imran over the worlds, and then Maryam from that family over the women of the worlds. The same verb of choosing ties them.
3:33|3:42.relation: The choice of the family, then of Maryam within it.

3:40|3:165.why: Only the question word how; Zakariya's wonder at a son versus the believers asking why defeat came. One word is too little.

3:52|3:160.why: Only the root of helping; Isa's disciples versus Allah's help in battle. Different subjects.

3:57|3:76.why: Only the closing about whom Allah loves or does not love, a stock pattern, and a shared root of paying in full. Different subjects.

3:62|3:126.why: Only the names Mighty and Wise. Different subjects.

cmp-card:3:67|3:95,3:70|3:98.why: Two different pairs: Ibrahim described as upright and not of the polytheists (3:67, 3:95), and the rebuke to the People of the Book for disbelieving in the signs (3:70, 3:98). Each pair is good, but they are two things.
cmp-card:3:67|3:95,3:70|3:98.changes: Split into the Ibrahim pair and the rebuke pair, since the card joins two unrelated matches.
cmp-card:3:67|3:95,3:70|3:98.relation: Ibrahim's true way, and the People of the Book rebuked for denying what they witness.

3:83|3:109.why: All in the heavens and earth belong to Allah and return to Him: in 3:83 they submit willingly or not, in 3:109 all matters go back to Him.
3:83|3:109.relation: Everything in creation submits to Allah and returns to Him.

3:86|3:101.why: Two questions of how: how would Allah guide those who disbelieved after belief, and how can you disbelieve while the signs are recited and the Messenger is among you.
3:86|3:101.relation: Disbelief after the proof has come, warned against in the same passage.

3:104|3:114.why: Enjoining good and forbidding evil: commanded of this nation in 3:104, praised in the upright among the People of the Book in 3:114. A memorizer pair with different endings.
3:104|3:114.relation: The same duty, as a command and as praise.

3:122|3:160.why: Both close with the call for the believers to rely on Allah: when two groups almost lost heart, and when victory is His alone.
3:122|3:160.relation: Reliance on Allah as the lesson of the battle.

3:130|3:200.why: Two commands to the believers, leaving usury and holding firm in patience, both closing with fear Allah so that you may succeed.
3:130|3:200.relation: Success tied to fearing Allah in wealth and in steadfastness.

3:157|3:169.why: Those killed in the way of Allah: forgiveness better than what people gather, and they are alive with their Lord.
3:157|3:169.relation: Same subject: what awaits those killed in Allah's way.

3:176|3:177.why: Consecutive ayat: those who hasten into disbelief, and those who buy disbelief for faith, will not harm Allah at all. Different closings of punishment.

3:189|15:19.why: Only the words all things. Different subjects.

3:177|17:10.why: Only painful punishment, a stock phrase. Different subjects.

3:35|21:4.why: Only the names Hearing and Knowing. Different subjects.

3:94|23:38.why: Only the common phrase inventing a lie against Allah; a general verdict versus a people accusing their messenger. Different uses.

3:169|23:117.why: Only the words with their Lord. Different subjects.

3:189|23:18.why: Only common words of heaven, earth and power. Different subjects.

3:57|26:227.why: Only the generic formula of those who believe and do good. Different subjects.

3:57|32:19.why: Only the generic formula of those who believe and do good, with different rewards. Stock phrase.

3:194|32:25.why: Only the words Day of Resurrection. Different subjects.

3:29|33:27.why: Only the stock closing about Allah's power. Different subjects.

3:31|33:73.why: Only the stock closing Forgiving, Merciful. Different subjects.

3:32|33:48.why: Only the words obey and disbelievers. Different subjects.

21:24|28:75.why:
The same challenge to the idolaters, once in this world and once on the Day of Judgment, and the truth they now ignore they then come to know:
هاتوا برهانكم
21:24|28:75.relation: Contrast: here most of them do not know the truth and turn away; on that Day they know the truth belongs to Allah.

21:69|28:53.why: Nothing shared but common words; the fire made cool for Ibrahim and the People of the Book believing in the Quran are unrelated.

21:10|29:51.why: Both say the Book sent down is itself the reminder they need, answering those who demand other signs.
21:10|29:51.relation: The revealed Book is a reminder and enough as a sign.

21:16|29:44.why: Two sides of one point about creation: the heavens and earth were not made in play, they were made in truth.
21:16|29:44.relation: Creation has a purpose: not play (21:16), but truth (29:44).

21:108|29:46.why: The same creed in the same words, told to the idolaters and to the People of the Book: your God is one, and we submit to Him.
21:108|29:46.relation: One message of oneness and submission, addressed to two audiences.

21:45|30:52.why: Near-identical clause with a different ending, a real trap for memorizers; both say the deniers cannot hear the warning, like the deaf.
21:45|30:52.relation: The deaf do not hear the call: when warned (21:45), when they turn their backs (30:52).

21:94|30:45.why: Only the stock phrase of good deeds is shared; the subjects (no effort is lost, and the reward from His grace) are generic.

21:29|31:11.why: Only the stock words for false gods and wrongdoers are shared; a claim to godhood punished and a challenge to show what idols created are different points.

21:81|33:27.why: Only a closing attribute about all things is shared; the wind for Sulayman and the land given after the Quraiza have nothing to compare.

21:81|33:54.why: Only the stock closing about knowing all things; the subjects are unrelated.

21:38|34:29.why: The same ayah word for word in two surahs; a memorizer must know where it recurs and what follows each time.
21:38|34:29.relation: The deniers' recurring taunt about the promised Hour.

21:55|34:49.why: Only the word truth is shared; Ibrahim's people asking if he is serious and the truth having come are different scenes.

21:4|35:38.why: Only the stock attribute of knowing the heavens and earth; nothing specific to compare.

21:28|36:9.why: Before them and behind them means different things: Allah's knowledge of the angels, and a barrier set on the deniers. Nothing to learn by comparing.

21:28|36:45.why: Only the phrase before and behind is shared; Allah's knowledge of the angels and a call to the deniers to fear are different subjects.

cmp-card:21:38|36:48,21:38|36:52.why: The taunt is repeated word for word in both surahs, and Ya-Sin then shows its answer at the resurrection, when the deniers admit the promise was true.
cmp-card:21:38|36:48,21:38|36:52.relation: Contrast: they mock when this promise comes; when raised they confess this is what the Merciful promised.

21:43|36:74.why: Both say the gods they take besides Allah cannot help. The next ayah 36:75 completes the match: they cannot help themselves (21:43), they cannot help their worshippers (36:75).
21:43|36:74.changes: Added 36:75 to the Ya-Sin row, since the matching statement that the gods are unable to help is there.
21:43|36:74.relation: False gods cannot give victory, neither to themselves nor to those who worship them.

21:4|37:5.why: Only the stock words Lord, heaven and earth; Allah hearing all speech and His lordship of the easts are different points.

21:16|37:5.why: Only the stock phrase the heavens, earth and what is between them; creation not in play and a divine title share no point.

cmp-card:21:52|37:85,21:53|37:85.why: The same scene in nearly the same words: Ibrahim asks his father and his people about what they worship. A memorizer must tell the two questions apart.
cmp-card:21:52|37:85,21:53|37:85.relation: One story told twice: Ibrahim confronting his father and people over their idols.

21:56|37:5.why: Only the common divine title Lord of the heavens and the earth is shared; Ibrahim's answer and the oath at the opening of as-Saffat are different contexts.

cmp-card:21:76|37:76,21:76|37:115.why: The same rescue from the great distress, said of Nuh in both surahs and of Musa and Harun; a memorizer must keep the wording apart. In as-Saffat the call of Nuh is in 37:75, which matches his call in 21:76.
cmp-card:21:76|37:76,21:76|37:115.changes: Added 37:75 to the Nuh row in as-Saffat: it has Nuh calling and being answered, matching 21:76, and names who was saved.
cmp-card:21:76|37:76,21:76|37:115.relation: Allah answers the call and saves His messengers from the great distress.

21:112|37:180.why: Only the stock ending about what they describe; a plea for judgment and a glorification are different.

21:4|38:66.why: Only the stock words Lord, heaven and earth; nothing specific shared.

21:16|38:10.why: Only the stock phrase the heavens, earth and what is between them; creation with purpose and a challenge to the deniers over dominion are different points.

21:16|38:66.why: Only the stock phrase the heavens, earth and what is between them; creation with purpose and a divine title share no point.

21:56|38:66.why: Only the common divine title Lord of the heavens and the earth is shared; Ibrahim's answer to his people and the Prophet's declaration in Sad are different contexts.

cmp-card:21:83|38:41,21:84|38:43.why: The story of Ayyub told twice in close wording: his call that harm touched him, and his family given back with as many again, as a mercy and a reminder. The endings differ (for the worshippers / for people of understanding), a point for memorizers.
cmp-card:21:83|38:41,21:84|38:43.relation: One story: Ayyub's patience in affliction, his call, and Allah's answer.

21:108|38:65.why: Both are commands to the Prophet to declare that there is only one God, in parallel openings; useful to compare how each is framed.
21:108|38:65.relation: The core message of oneness, declared by the Prophet in two ways.

21:4|39:44.why: Only the heavens and the earth are shared; Allah hearing all speech and intercession belonging to Him are different points.

21:41|39:48.why: The same closing clause: what they mocked closed in on them. Once of earlier nations, once on the Day of Judgment.
21:41|39:48.relation: Mockery of the warning returns on the mockers, in this world and the next.

21:56|39:44.why: Only the heavens and the earth are shared; the Lord who created them and intercession belonging to Allah are different points.

21:41|40:83.why: The same end for those who mocked their messengers: what they mocked closed in on them.
21:41|40:83.relation: Mockery of the messengers returns on the mockers.

21:52|40:30.why: Only a speaker addressing his people is shared; Ibrahim on the idols and the believer of Pharaoh's family warning of the fate of the confederates are different subjects.

21:20|41:38.why: The same picture of the angels glorifying night and day without tiring, in two wordings a memorizer must keep apart.
21:20|41:38.relation: Those near Allah never tire of glorifying Him, while the proud refuse to bow.

21:108|41:6.why: The same revealed sentence, your God is one God, with different openings and endings; a clear trap for memorizers.
21:108|41:6.relation: The one message revealed to the Prophet, and the response asked for: submit, or go straight to Him and seek forgiveness.

21:81|42:12.why: Only the stock closing about all things; the subjects are unrelated.

21:4|43:9.why: Only the heavens, the earth and the Knowing are shared; nothing specific to compare.

21:4|43:82.why: Only the stock words Lord, heaven and earth; different subjects.

21:4|43:84.why: Only the heaven, the earth and the Knowing are shared; Allah hearing all speech and being God in heaven and earth are different points.

21:16|43:9.why: Only the common phrase about creating the heavens and the earth; creation not in play and the deniers' admission of the Creator are different points.

21:25|43:45.why: Both appeal to all the messengers sent before: every one was told to worship Allah alone, so ask them whether any other god was given.
21:25|43:45.relation: Every messenger before brought the same message of oneness.

21:26|43:20.why: Only the deniers' words about the Merciful are shared; the claim that He took a son and the excuse that He willed their worship are different points.

21:26|43:81.why: The same false claim, that the Merciful has a son, answered in two ways.
21:26|43:81.relation: Answers to the claim of a son: they are honoured servants (21:26); were it so, I would be the first to worship (43:81).

21:31|43:10.why: The same sign in close wording: ways made in the earth so that people may be guided. Useful for memorizers and for reflecting on the twofold guidance, on roads and to Allah.
21:31|43:10.relation: Paths in the earth as a sign that guides.

21:33|43:12.why: Only the words who created and all are shared; the orbits of sun and moon and the creation of pairs and mounts are different signs.

21:52|43:26.why: The same opening of Ibrahim's speech to his father and his people, in two surahs: once questioning the idols, once declaring himself free of them.
21:52|43:26.relation: One story: Ibrahim confronting his father and people, questioning and then disowning.

cmp-card:21:53|43:22,21:53|43:24.why: The same excuse of following the fathers, given to Ibrahim and to every messenger, and the messenger's answer.
cmp-card:21:53|43:22,21:53|43:24.relation: Blind following of forefathers as the deniers' excuse, and the call to something better guided.

21:53|43:26.why: Same story, but the rows do not match: one is the people's reply, the other Ibrahim's disowning. The pairs 21:52 with 43:26 and 21:53 with 43:22 already show the parallel.

21:54|43:40.why: Only the stock phrase clear error is shared; different subjects.

21:55|43:30.why: Only the word truth and a reply are shared; the two answers to the messenger differ in meaning and wording.

21:56|43:82.why: Only the common title Lord of the heavens and the earth is shared; different contexts.

21:103|43:83.why: The same phrase, the Day they are promised, closes both: the believers are met by angels on it, the deniers are left to play until they meet it.
21:103|43:83.relation: Contrast: one promised Day, met in peace by the believers and in dread by the deniers.

21:112|43:82.why: Only the stock ending about what they describe; a plea for judgment and a glorification are different.

21:4|44:6.why: Only the stock closing the Hearing, the Knowing; different subjects.

21:4|44:7.why: Only the stock words Lord, heaven and earth; different subjects.

21:16|44:7.why: Only the stock phrase the heavens, earth and what is between them; different points.

21:56|44:7.why: Only the common title Lord of the heavens and the earth is shared; different contexts.

21:4|45:36.why: Only the stock words Lord, heaven and earth; different subjects.

21:41|45:33.why: The same closing clause: what they mocked closed in on them. The deeds wording here (what they did) differs from 39:48 (what they earned), a point for memorizers.
21:41|45:33.relation: Mockery of the warning returns on the mockers.

21:56|45:36.why: Only the common title Lord of the heavens and the earth is shared; different contexts.

21:16|46:3.why: The same statement about creation in near-identical wording: not in play (21:16), but in truth and for a fixed term (46:3).
21:16|46:3.relation: Creation has a purpose and an end.

21:30|46:33.why: Both open with the same rebuke to the deniers and point to the creation of the heavens and earth as proof of His power over life.
21:30|46:33.relation: Have they not seen: creation as the proof of giving life and raising the dead.

21:38|46:22.why: The same defiant demand by deniers in two ages: bring what you promise us, if you are truthful.
21:38|46:22.relation: Deniers of every age challenge the messenger to bring the threatened punishment.

21:78|48:19.why: Only words from the same root as judgment and wisdom; Dawud and Sulayman's ruling and the spoils of war are unrelated.

21:4|49:16.why: Only the stock statement that Allah knows what is in the heavens and earth; different subjects.

21:4|49:18.why: Only the stock statement of Allah's knowledge of the heavens and earth; different subjects.

21:16|50:38.why: The same creation of the heavens, earth and what is between them, with two denials: not in play, and with no fatigue.
