21:16|50:38.relation: Creation done with purpose and without weariness.

21:4|51:23.why: Only the words Lord, heaven and earth; Allah hearing speech and an oath on the truth of provision are different.

21:56|51:23.why: Only the common title Lord of the heaven and earth; different contexts.

21:16|52:36.why: Only the creation of the heavens and earth is shared; creation not in play and the question whether they created them are different points.

21:4|64:4.why: Both say Allah knows all speech, secret and open, in heaven and earth; 21:4 answers the deniers' secret talk in 21:3.
21:4|64:4.relation: Nothing said in secret is hidden from Allah.

21:16|64:3.why: Two sides of one point about creation: the heavens and earth were not made in play, they were made in truth.
21:16|64:3.relation: Creation has a purpose: not play, but truth.

21:36|67:28.why: Only the word disbelievers and seeing are shared; the deniers mocking the Prophet and the question who will protect them are different points.

21:38|67:25.why: The same ayah word for word in two surahs; a memorizer must know where it recurs and what follows each time.
21:38|67:25.relation: The deniers' recurring taunt about the promised Hour.

21:49|67:12.why: The same description of the believers, those who fear their Lord unseen, with two endings: their dread of the Hour, and their forgiveness and reward.
21:49|67:12.relation: Fearing Allah unseen: its sign and its reward.

21:54|67:29.why: Only the stock phrase clear error is shared; Ibrahim's charge to his people and the Prophet's declaration of trust are different points.

21:61|67:30.why: Only the verb bring is shared; different subjects.

21:60|68:51.why: Only hearing and mention are shared; different subjects.

cmp-card:21:103|70:42,21:103|70:44.why: The promised Day closes all three: the believers are met by angels on it; the deniers are left to play until they meet it, then come humbled.
cmp-card:21:103|70:42,21:103|70:44.relation: Contrast: one promised Day, met in peace by the believers and in humiliation by the deniers.

21:42|71:5.why: Only night and day are shared; different subjects.

21:4|78:37.why: Only the words Lord, heaven and earth; different subjects.

21:16|78:37.why: Only the stock phrase the heavens, earth and what is between them; different points.

21:56|78:37.why: Only the common title Lord of the heavens and the earth is shared; different contexts.

21:56|85:9.why: Only the heavens, earth and the word witness are shared; different points.

21:73|98:5.why: The prophets of Ibrahim's line were inspired to pray, give zakat and worship Allah, and the People of the Book were commanded nothing other than this; the upright religion is the same.
21:73|98:5.relation: The religion of the prophets is the one the People of the Book were commanded.

22:3|22:8.why: The same opening in one surah, a few ayat apart, with different continuations; a clear trap for memorizers.
22:3|22:8.relation: Two kinds of disputers about Allah without knowledge: the follower of every devil, and the proud leader without guidance or book.

22:6|22:74.why: Only words from the same roots are shared; different points.

22:8|22:68.why: In one surah: there are those who dispute about Allah without knowledge, and the Prophet is told how to answer them.
22:8|22:68.relation: Disputing about Allah, and the answer: Allah knows best what you do.

22:12|22:62.why: What they call on besides Allah is described twice in one surah: it neither harms nor benefits, it is falsehood.
22:12|22:62.relation: The emptiness of what is worshipped besides Allah, against Allah who is the Truth.

cmp-card:22:14|22:23,22:14|22:56.why: 22:14 and 22:23 open identically and differ in their endings, a real trap for memorizers; 22:56 gives the same promise on the Day Allah judges.
cmp-card:22:14|22:23,22:14|22:56.relation: The believers' reward, promised in one surah three times.

22:61|22:75.why: Only the stock closing the Hearing, the Seeing is shared; the alternation of night and day and the choosing of messengers are different subjects.

22:63|23:18.why: The same sign of water sent down from the sky to the earth, shown from two sides: it makes the earth green, and He could take it away.
22:63|23:18.relation: Rain as a sign of His kindness and His power.

22:66|23:37.why: Life, death and life again stated by Allah, and denied by the disbelievers in the same words.
22:66|23:37.relation: Contrast: He gives life, causes death and gives life again; they say we die and live and will not be raised.

cmp-card:22:16|24:1,22:16|24:34,22:16|24.why: The same statement, We sent down clear signs, with different endings; 22:16 and 24:46 both close with Allah guiding whom He wills.
cmp-card:22:16|24:1,22:16|24:34,22:16|24.relation: Clear signs are sent down, and guidance is from Allah.

22:61|24:44.why: The same sign of Allah alternating night and day, with a call to reflect on it.
22:61|24:44.relation: The turning of night and day as a sign of His power.

22:63|24:41.why: Only the opening do you not see that Allah is shared; rain and the glorification of all creatures are different signs.

22:69|24:48.why: Only judging between them is shared; Allah's judgment on the Day and the hypocrites refusing the Messenger's judgment are different.

22:70|24:64.why: Both close a passage with Allah's knowledge of all in the heavens and earth, and of what people do.
22:70|24:64.relation: Allah knows all, and all is recorded and will be told.

22:14|25:70.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds; gardens and sins turned to good deeds are different points.

22:66|25:49.why: Only life and death words are shared; human life and death and rain reviving land are different subjects.

22:67|25:31.why: Only the words every and We made, and Lord with guidance; rites for each nation and enemies for each prophet are different points.

cmp-card:22:70|27:25,22:70|27:65,22:70|2.why: Allah's knowledge of what is hidden in the heavens and the earth; 22:70 and 27:75 both add that it is recorded in a book.
cmp-card:22:70|27:25,22:70|27:65,22:70|2.relation: Nothing hidden in heaven or earth escapes His knowledge or His record.

22:50|28:67.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds; different subjects.

22:12|29:42.why: Only what they call on besides Allah is shared; the point of each ayah differs (no harm or benefit; Allah knows them).

cmp-card:22:14|29:58,22:23|29:58,22:56|2.why: Across the surahs only the general reward formula is shared: those who believe and do good, gardens with rivers. Nothing specific links al-Ankabut to al-Hajj here; the strong match of 22:14 with 22:23 is already its own card.

22:50|29:9.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds; the rewards named differ.

22:57|29:23.why: Only the general statement that deniers of the signs have punishment; nothing specific to compare.

22:62|29:42.why: The same clause about what they call on besides Him, and the same verdict: it is falsehood (22:62), it is nothing (29:42).
22:62|29:42.relation: What is worshipped besides Allah is nothing at all.

22:70|29:52.why: Only the stock statement that Allah knows what is in the heavens and the earth; the surrounding points differ.

22:6|30:50.why: Nearly the same closing: He gives life to the dead and is able over all things. In 30:50 it follows rain reviving the land, the proof of resurrection.
22:6|30:50.relation: Reviving the dead earth as proof of reviving the dead.

22:8|30:29.why: Only the phrase without knowledge is shared; disputing about Allah and following desires are different points.

22:38|30:45.why: Only the stock statement that Allah does not love the disbelievers; different subjects.

22:50|30:15.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds; the rewards named differ.

22:50|30:45.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds; different subjects.

22:57|30:16.why: The same wording for the deniers' end, and in both surahs it follows straight after the believers' reward; a memorizer must keep the endings apart.
22:57|30:16.relation: Contrast: the believers in gardens, the deniers of the signs in punishment.

22:12|31:11.why: Only besides Allah and error are shared; different points.

22:12|31:30.why: What they call on besides Allah: it neither harms nor benefits (22:12), it is falsehood (31:30).
22:12|31:30.relation: The emptiness of what is worshipped besides Allah.

22:41|31:17.why: The same duties: establish prayer, enjoin good and forbid evil. Once as the mark of those given power, once in Luqman's advice to his son.
22:41|31:17.relation: The same duties, for the ruler and for the young believer, each closed with a word about affairs.

22:50|31:8.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds; the rewards named differ.

22:56|31:8.why: The same promise in close wording: those who believe and do good are in the Gardens of Bliss. Close enough to confuse a memorizer.
22:56|31:8.relation: The believers' reward, the Gardens of Bliss.

cmp-card:22:61|31:29,22:62|31:30.why: Two consecutive ayat repeated almost word for word in two surahs, with different endings; a key passage for memorizers.
cmp-card:22:61|31:29,22:62|31:30.relation: The alternation of night and day, and Allah as the Truth against the falsehood of other gods.

22:64|31:25.why: Only the heavens, earth and praise are shared; different points.

22:74|31:9.why: Only the words Allah, truth and Mighty; different subjects.

22:75|31:28.why: Only the stock closing the Hearing, the Seeing is shared; different subjects.

22:50|32:19.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds; the rewards named differ.

22:56|32:19.why: Only the stock formula of faith and good deeds with gardens; the names of the gardens and the contexts differ.

22:69|32:25.why: The same statement in close wording: on the Day of Resurrection Allah judges between them in what they differed. A memorizer must tell the openings apart.
22:69|32:25.relation: All disputes are settled by Allah on the Day of Resurrection.

22:6|33:27.why: Only the stock closing able over all things; different subjects.

22:50|33:31.why: Only noble provision and good deeds are shared; the reward of believers and of the Prophet's wives are different contexts.

22:63|33:34.why: Only the stock closing Subtle, Aware; different subjects.

22:44|34:45.why: Both close with the same question after earlier nations denied: then how was My rejection.
22:44|34:45.relation: The end of those who denied the messengers before.

cmp-card:22:50|34:4,22:51|34:5,22:54|34:.why: Three matching ayat in the same order: the believers' forgiveness and noble provision, those who strive against the signs, and those given knowledge seeing it is the truth. A strong parallel for memorizers and for pondering.
cmp-card:22:50|34:4,22:51|34:5,22:54|34:.relation: One sequence in two surahs: the believers' reward, the opponents' end, and the knowers' recognition of the truth.

22:51|34:38.why: The same description of those who strive to defeat Our signs, with two endings a memorizer must keep apart.
22:51|34:38.relation: The end of those who strive against the signs.

22:63|34:1.why: Only heaven, earth and Aware; different points.

22:64|34:1.why: The same statement that all in the heavens and the earth is His, joined to praise.
22:64|34:1.relation: Owner of all, and so the Praised.

22:44|35:26.why: The same words: then I seized them, and how was My rejection.
22:44|35:26.relation: The end of those who denied the messengers.

22:50|35:7.why: Close wording a memorizer can confuse: forgiveness and noble provision (22:50), forgiveness and a great reward (35:7). Both set the believers against the deniers.
22:50|35:7.relation: The believers' forgiveness and reward, beside the deniers' punishment.

22:61|35:13.why: The same words for the alternation of night and day; 35:13 also matches 31:29 with the sun and moon.
22:61|35:13.relation: The turning of night and day as a sign of His power.

22:64|35:15.why: Only the stock closing the Rich, the Praised is shared; His ownership and people's need of Him are different points.

22:70|35:38.why: Only the stock statement of Allah's knowledge of the heavens and earth; nothing specific shared.

22:76|35:4.why: Only the stock closing that matters return to Allah is shared; different subjects.

22:6|36:12.why: Both declare that Allah gives life to the dead, and close with His power or His record of all things.
22:6|36:12.relation: Giving life to the dead, and all things counted.

22:76|36:9.why: Before them and behind them means different things: Allah's knowledge and a barrier set on the deniers.

22:76|36:45.why: Only the phrase before and behind is shared; different subjects.

4:11|4:12.why: The inheritance law repeats the same condition in both ayat: every share is paid only after a bequest or debt is settled. A memorizer must track the varying verb form in each place.
4:11|4:12.relation: The same condition runs through all the shares of the inheritance law.

20:71|26:49.why: Same scene told twice: Pharaoh threatens the magicians who believed. The wording is near identical, with differences to note: an added warning in 26:49, and a different end to the threat in each.
20:71|26:49.relation: One event in two surahs: the believing magicians facing Pharaoh's threat.

tree:07qgkrr1sv87e3.why: Same declaration of Allah's dominion opening three ayat, each continuing differently; 2:107 and 9:116 both end with no protector or helper besides Allah, while 5:40 speaks of punishing and forgiving. Useful for a memorizer.

tree:093abcj0r9hgxx.why: The deniers' same question about being raised after becoming dust and bones, in four places; 37:53 alone ends with being judged instead of raised. Classic memorizer trap, and one theme: denial of resurrection.
tree:093abcj0r9hgxx.relation: The same disbelief in resurrection, answered differently in each surah.

tree:0gujjom0e2n2nu.why: A stock closing formula on Allah's power, shared by unrelated ayat on many subjects. Nothing to learn from seeing these together; it is a search, not a card.

tree:1ql64tj1p4g0vl.why: The same list of patriarchs in two nearby ayat of al-Baqara: in 2:136 the believers declare faith in what was revealed to them, in 2:140 Jews and Christians are refuted for claiming them as their own.
tree:1ql64tj1p4g0vl.changes: Add 3:84 and 4:163, which carry the same list; 3:84 is the classic twin of 2:136. They sit in another card only because the name is spelled differently in the script.
tree:1ql64tj1p4g0vl.relation: Contrast: the list as an object of faith versus the list as a disputed claim.

tree:1b2fybp1y0ncvd.why: The same list of patriarchs: 3:84 is the declaration of faith in all revelation, 4:163 lists those to whom Allah revealed as He revealed to the Prophet.
tree:1b2fybp1y0ncvd.changes: Add 2:136 and 2:140, which carry the same list; 2:136 is the classic twin of 3:84. They sit in another card only because the name is spelled differently in the script.
tree:1b2fybp1y0ncvd.relation: One chain of revelation, stated as faith in 3:84 and as Allah's act in 4:163.

17:89|25:50.why: Same statement that Allah varied the reminders for people and most refused all but disbelief. Two wordings of the first half to keep apart.
17:89|25:50.relation: The same complaint about people's refusal despite varied reminders.

tree:1gyr70d19kyrfp.why: Both ayat show the worthlessness of protectors taken besides Allah: in 29:41 as a spider's flimsy house, in 45:10 as nothing that will avail them before Hell.
tree:1gyr70d19kyrfp.relation: The weakness of false protectors, shown by a parable and by the Hereafter.

tree:0b3giaq1prpnwq.why: A rare full clause, fear Allah to whom you will be gathered, closing a command in only these two places (hunting in ihram, and secret counsel). Useful for a memorizer even though the subjects differ.

tree:1u6tjut1ekdgdv.why: The same exhortation, fear Allah if you are believers, in only these two places, both in al-Ma'ida: once to the believers, once from Jesus to the disciples asking for the table. Useful for a memorizer.

16:96|16:97.why: Two neighbouring ayat end with the same promise of being rewarded by the best of what they did, the first for the patient, the second for every believer who does good. A memorizer needs to see them together.
16:96|16:97.relation: The same reward promised to the patient and to every believing doer of good.

21:52|26:70.why: Same scene: Abraham questions his father and people about their worship. The question is worded fully in 21:52 and briefly in 26:70.
21:52|26:70.relation: One event told in two surahs.

8:45|62:10.why: The same command to remember Allah much that you may succeed, once in the face of the enemy and once in the market after Friday prayer.
8:45|62:10.relation: Remembrance asked for both in battle and in daily trade.

tree:0izljco02tepd2.why: Both call the believers to remember Allah's favour, then name a specific event: hearts joined after enmity in 3:103, enemies' hands held back in 5:11.
tree:0izljco02tepd2.relation: Allah's favour remembered through concrete events of protection and unity.

24:6|24:8.why: The two sides of the same oath procedure between spouses: the husband swears he is truthful, the wife swears he is lying.
24:6|24:8.relation: Mirror oaths in one law: truthful against lying.

tree:0h4czjg07akbr8.why: The same command to seek refuge in Allah with two different closing names: the Hearing, the Seeing in 40:56 and the Hearing, the Knowing in 41:36. A classic memorizer pair in neighbouring surahs.

tree:068mgkx12p78ln.why: The same scene of the wrongdoers hiding regret when they see the punishment, continued differently: judgment with justice in 10:54, chains on necks in 34:33.
tree:068mgkx12p78ln.relation: The same moment of regret on seeing the punishment.

tree:182re8v0bcjt1h.why: The same description of whoever submits his face to Allah while doing good: in 2:112 he has his reward, in 4:125 he follows the way of Abraham.
tree:182re8v0bcjt1h.relation: Two consequences of the same submission: reward, and the best of religion.

24:54|64:12.why: Same command to obey Allah and the Messenger, then if they turn away, his duty is only clear delivery. Wording differs in the middle, which a memorizer must keep apart.
24:54|64:12.relation: The same rule on the Messenger's duty in two surahs.

39:2|39:11.why: Within one surah: Allah commands the Prophet to worship Him with sincere religion, then the Prophet declares he was commanded exactly that.
39:2|39:11.relation: A command and the Prophet's own declaration of it.

58:15|65:10.why: The same threat of severe punishment prepared by Allah, opening an ayah in two neighbouring surahs, with different continuations. Useful for a memorizer.

tree:1bn93d503lg897.why: The same prayer for forgiveness and mercy ending differently: best of forgivers in 7:155 (Moses), best of the merciful in 23:109 (the believers).
tree:1bn93d503lg897.relation: One prayer in the mouth of Moses and of the believers.

tree:1d26o6l0egsjoh.why: The same command to pray, give alms and obey, then the object differs: the Messenger in 24:56, Allah and His Messenger in 58:13. A memorizer pair.

5:62|5:63.why: Two consecutive ayat on the same people and their eating of the unlawful, ending with what they used to do and what they used to work, a classic memorizer difference.
5:62|5:63.relation: Blame on the sinners, then on the scholars who did not forbid them.

tree:0cl2p6a1vk0fs4.why: Both protect wives from being pressured or put out of their homes, with the same single exception of open immorality. Same subject in two laws.
tree:0cl2p6a1vk0fs4.relation: The one exception that lifts a wife's protection, in marriage and in divorce.

tree:1h9pavb1je4zwd.why: The same exception on the Day: none speaks or intercedes except whom the Most Merciful permits, ending with being pleased with his word in 20:109 and speaking what is right in 78:38.
tree:1h9pavb1je4zwd.relation: Permission to speak on the Day of Judgment, described from two sides.

tree:0ayjze714u3fud.why: Both address all mankind and ground the oneness of Allah in His dominion over heavens and earth, then draw a different conclusion: believe in the Messenger, or how are you turned away. The shared part beyond the stock phrase is thin.
tree:0ayjze714u3fud.relation: Two calls to mankind arguing from creation to the oneness of Allah.

tree:0t8fdyr1p0grf1.why: What was revealed to the Prophet from his Lord is the truth: most people do not believe it (13:1), while those given knowledge see it (34:6).
tree:0t8fdyr1p0grf1.relation: Contrast: most people reject the revelation, the knowledgeable recognise it.

tree:10t511x0lxgep9.why: The creation of mankind from a single soul and its mate, told with two different verbs for making the mate. A classic memorizer pair, and one theme.
tree:10t511x0lxgep9.relation: The same origin of mankind, told as a call to piety and as a story of the first couple.

32:19|95:6.why: Only the stock formula of those who believe and do good with their reward; the contexts are unrelated and nothing is learned from the pair.

tree:1qxo81v1cpfuup.why: Both picture the Day of Judgment sorting people, with the believers placed in gardens named differently in each. The formula is common but the setting is shared.
tree:1qxo81v1cpfuup.relation: The believers' place in the judgment scene, named two ways.

tree:0tt11ka0oghls2.why: The shared word after the formula is a different word in each: from His bounty in 30:45, out of darkness in 65:11. Beyond that only the stock formula is shared.

tree:1nlm1a91h3cmel.why: Both show the gods taken besides Allah failing those who took them: a spider's flimsy house in 29:41, gods who abandoned their worshippers in 46:28.
tree:1nlm1a91h3cmel.relation: The helplessness of false gods, by parable and by history.

tree:0gu476k1fzzn1i.why: The same opening about those who took protectors besides Him, continued differently: their excuse that the idols bring them near in 39:3, Allah watching over them in 42:6. A memorizer pair.
tree:0gu476k1fzzn1i.relation: The idolaters' claim and Allah's watch over them.

tree:1pj1ndd0il2p7x.why: The same phrase about those worshipped besides Allah: the Prophet refuses to worship them (10:104), and Abraham shows they cannot provide (29:17).
tree:1pj1ndd0il2p7x.relation: Refusing false worship, and the reason: they own nothing.

6:159|30:32.why: The same rare clause about those who split their religion into sects, with different conclusions: the Prophet has nothing to do with them, and each faction rejoices in its own.
6:159|30:32.relation: The danger of sectarian division, stated twice.

tree:05904vz1rqdxo1.why: Both speak of those killed in Allah's cause and promise them a gain: they are alive with their Lord (3:169), their deeds are not lost (47:4).

7:64|21:77.why: Same story: Noah saved and the people who denied Our signs drowned, with a different description of the people in each surah.
7:64|21:77.relation: One event, Noah's people drowned, in two surahs.

tree:1oqqi7g0j5k6em.why: Close neighbours in al-A'raf with the same subject, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant, and two consequences: the Fire, and the gates of heaven closed to them.
tree:1oqqi7g0j5k6em.relation: Two fates of the arrogant deniers.

tree:15tkk440wl09v2.why: The same threat of painful punishment for the disbelievers among them, introduced by two different verbs. A memorizer pair.

tree:1wss4dm0vmt39m.why: Two neighbouring ayat on those who do not believe in Allah's signs: Allah does not guide them, and they are the ones who invent lies.
tree:1wss4dm0vmt39m.relation: The deniers described twice in a row: unguided, and the true liars.

tree:1rexad208e12qk.why: Both end with the aim of becoming God-fearing and mention those before you: worship of the Creator in 2:21, fasting in 2:183.
tree:1rexad208e12qk.relation: Piety as the aim of both worship and fasting.

tree:1r7wmu802esyb2.why: Those they call on besides Him answer nothing (13:14) and judge nothing (40:20), each set against Allah's true call or true judgment.
tree:1r7wmu802esyb2.relation: The false gods' helplessness against Allah's truth.

4:115|47:32.why: A rare clause: opposing the Messenger after guidance has become clear, with the consequence in each. Same subject.
4:115|47:32.relation: The fate of those who oppose the Messenger knowingly.

tree:1iezmus11979tg.why: The sun, moon and stars subjected by His command, as part of creation in 7:54 and as a sign for those who reason in 16:12.
tree:1iezmus11979tg.relation: The same cosmic order seen as Allah's creation and as a sign.

tree:1wyq6g01bpu00i.why: Only the stock closing that there are signs in that is shared; the word before it belongs to different phrases, and the subjects (Moses' mission, birds in the sky) are unrelated.

tree:0h3bjpp1ux09wt.why: Allah is the creator of all things, closing with two different attributes: the One, the Subduer in 13:16, and Guardian over all things in 39:62. A memorizer pair.
tree:0h3bjpp1ux09wt.relation: From creation of all things to two attributes of Allah.

tree:1xzr1910kze2br.why: Two agreements sealed by making Allah the guarantor of what is said: Jacob with his sons, and Moses with the old man of Madyan.
tree:1xzr1910kze2br.relation: Covenants witnessed by Allah in two prophets' lives.

tree:1u9sjv20gfwnyi.why: Allah begins creation then repeats it, closed differently: how are you deluded in 10:34, then to Him you return in 30:11.
tree:1u9sjv20gfwnyi.relation: Resurrection argued from the first creation.

tree:0m80mmy1rmsqao.why: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection: between the believers and the hypocrites in 4:141, over what you differed in at 22:69. Two continuations to keep apart.
tree:0m80mmy1rmsqao.relation: Disputes left to Allah's judgment on the Last Day.

tree:1x3yozo0v96jy8.why: The same list of the oppressed men, women and children in one surah: in 4:75 the believers must fight for them, in 4:98 they are excused from emigrating.
tree:1x3yozo0v96jy8.relation: The weak among the believers: a duty to defend them and an excuse granted to them.

tree:0h9kqaq1lpe8rk.why: The same rebuke said to the deniers in Hell: the Fire you used to deny, introduced differently in each place. Same scene and a memorizer pair.
tree:0h9kqaq1lpe8rk.relation: The deniers faced with the very Fire they denied.

tree:0mxu35c1olq4n8.why: The blessed land appears twice in al-Anbiya': Abraham and Lot saved to it, and the wind carrying Solomon's command to it. Same surah, different endings.
tree:0mxu35c1olq4n8.relation: One blessed land in two prophets' stories.

tree:0zik2ph0ev2egj.why: Revelation came to the Prophet and to those before him: in 39:65 with the warning against associating partners, in 42:3 as Allah's way of revealing. Neighbouring surahs.
tree:0zik2ph0ev2egj.relation: One revelation shared by all prophets.

tree:1jel2fy13nqdk4.why: Noah (10:72) and the Prophet (27:91) each declare they were commanded to be among those who submit, after different lead-ins.
tree:1jel2fy13nqdk4.relation: Two prophets with the same declaration of submission.

7:159|7:181.why: Same rare description of a community that guides by the truth and does justice by it: among the people of Moses, and among those We created.
7:159|7:181.relation: The righteous community, first among Moses' people and then in general.

tree:10m8th30ahtqw3.why: The same closing threat to the wrongdoers ends two ayat about false partners: Satan disowning those who associated him with Allah, and partners who legislated religion without Allah's leave.
tree:10m8th30ahtqw3.relation: Association of partners and its punishment.

tree:1nst4dy1tzpi08.why: A closing found only in these two places: Allah is kind and merciful to people, after the change of qibla in 2:143 and after the subjection of earth and sea in 22:65. Useful for a memorizer.

tree:07ga1531uemb5x.why: Allah does not love every one of a kind: the treacherous ingrate (22:38) and the arrogant boaster (31:18). A memorizer pair with two different types named.
tree:07ga1531uemb5x.relation: Two kinds of people Allah does not love.

tree:1re3oht1h7hmzd.why: Allah does not break His promise, said by the believers about the Day of gathering in 3:9 and by Allah about His promise coming upon the deniers in 13:31.
tree:1re3oht1h7hmzd.relation: Allah's promise, trusted by the believers and awaiting the deniers.

8:51|22:10.why: The same sentence to the punished: that is for what your hands sent ahead, and Allah is never unjust to His servants. A memorizer pair, with a singular and plural for hands.
8:51|22:10.changes: Add 3:182, which carries the same sentence word for word as 8:51.
8:51|22:10.relation: Punishment as the fruit of one's own deeds.

tree:0udsezd1b784qr.why: Two places in at-Tawba close with Allah being the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful: about accepting repentance and charity, and about the three who stayed behind.
tree:0udsezd1b784qr.relation: Allah's acceptance of repentance in the same surah of repentance.

tree:0b2ab5e124qt0c.why: Deniers tell the believers or the warners that they are only in error, with different adjectives: clear in 36:47, great in 67:9.
tree:0b2ab5e124qt0c.relation: The deniers accusing the guided of error.

tree:0bc3rhs0xpgkuy.why: If they turn away, the Prophet's duty is only to deliver: closing with Allah seeing His servants in 3:20 and with clear delivery in 16:82.
tree:0bc3rhs0xpgkuy.relation: The Prophet's duty limited to delivering the message.

tree:0q1k9ym06e0d0s.why: Patience is called a matter of firm resolve both to the believers under trial (3:186) and in Luqman's advice to his son (31:17).
tree:0q1k9ym06e0d0s.relation: Patience under hardship as true resolve.

tree:0n1nlzn0ghaofl.why: The rare singular form, a sign for the believers, closes only these two ayat (the ruins of Lot's people, and creation of the heavens). Useful for a memorizer against the common plural.

tree:0vzhnc91h760gl.why: Two adjacent ayat set out the witness's test in Joseph's story: the shirt torn from the front or from the back, with the verdict reversed.
tree:0vzhnc91h760gl.relation: A test by evidence with two mirror outcomes.

tree:1jc0l4k0v35yze.why: Two adjacent offers to bring the Queen's throne to Solomon: the jinn before he rises, the one with knowledge of the Book before the glance returns.
tree:1jc0l4k0v35yze.relation: Contrast: the power of the jinn against the power of knowledge.

13:1|13:19.why: In one surah, what was revealed to the Prophet is the truth: most people do not believe (13:1), and the one who knows it is not like the blind (13:19).
13:1|13:19.relation: Knowing the revelation is truth, and the blindness of those who do not.

tree:1dl7zej13i2jbh.why: After destroying past nations Allah raised up another generation; the same phrase in 6:6 and 23:31 with a different linking word.
tree:1dl7zej13i2jbh.relation: The succession of nations after destruction.

10:39|28:40.why: The warning to see the end of the wrongdoers follows denial of the Quran in 10:39 and Pharaoh's drowning in 28:40.
10:39|28:40.relation: The end of wrongdoers as a lesson.

7:103|27:14.why: Both close a passage on Moses and Pharaoh with the same call to see the end of the corrupters. Same story.
7:103|27:14.relation: Pharaoh's end as the lesson on corruption.

10:73|37:73.why: The same call to see the end of those warned, after Noah's people were drowned in 10:73 and after past warned nations in 37:73.
10:73|37:73.relation: The end of the warned nations who denied.

52:16|66:7.why: The same sentence said to the disbelievers in the Fire: you are only repaid for what you did, after telling them patience or excuses are useless.
52:16|66:7.relation: No excuse helps on the Day: only deeds are repaid.

tree:0950ljn1i1dxrx.why: Only the generic frame 'and they, in it, do not ...' is shared. The subjects differ (worldly seekers paid in full in this life vs the people of Hell who cannot hear) and the verbs differ, so there is nothing to confuse or to ponder.

tree:0auafnl0ztb5fn.why: A real mutashabih in two neighbouring surahs: the same verdict on the deniers ends both ayat, opened once with 'rather' and once with 'or'. Easy to swap when reciting.
tree:0auafnl0ztb5fn.relation: Same charge against the deniers of the messenger: transgression, not reason, drives them.

tree:0iefw0a1y7qohm.why: Both ayat are about dying while a disbeliever and what then awaits: curse in 2:161, prepared punishment in 4:18. Same theme, close wording, worth holding together.
tree:0iefw0a1y7qohm.relation: Death in disbelief closes the door: no repentance at the last moment (4:18), only the curse (2:161).

tree:1lfhjk31qhdgtn.why: Strong mutashabih: both open with the disbelievers who die as disbelievers, then 'nothing will be accepted' (3:91) vs 'God will not forgive them' (47:34). Same theme, different consequence to remember.
tree:1lfhjk31qhdgtn.relation: Death in disbelief: no ransom accepted and no forgiveness.

tree:0z434wk1yzqt84.why: Same ayah-final clause, opened with 'and' in 7:198 and 'so' in 36:9. Both describe people who face the guidance yet cannot see it, which is a theme worth pondering, and the opening letter is the memorizer's trap.
tree:0z434wk1yzqt84.relation: Blindness to guidance: looking without seeing (7:198), veiled by a barrier (36:9).

tree:132t83w0ythhnm.why: Both are prostration ayat ending 'and they are not arrogant': the angels and all creatures in 16:49, the believers in 32:15. The believers are described with the angels' quality.
tree:132t83w0ythhnm.relation: Similarity: humble prostration joins the believers to the angels.

tree:1wzoso71lcnbmr.why: A striking contrast in the same words: Joseph knew his brothers while they did not know him (12:58); the deniers know their messenger yet act as if they did not (23:69). The opening letter differs (and/so).
tree:1wzoso71lcnbmr.relation: Contrast: not recognizing out of ignorance vs denying what is known.

tree:1uom7cp0hnn55p.why: Same story, same closing, father and son: Jacob entrusts Benjamin to God (12:64) and Joseph forgives his brothers (12:92), both ending with God as the most merciful of the merciful.
tree:1uom7cp0hnn55p.relation: Jacob's trust and Joseph's forgiveness rest on the same faith in God's mercy.

tree:0ise1yk0k2rvb0.why: Only 'He knows best what' is shared, a common phrase. One ayah is about the reckoning on the Day of Judgement, the other about the charge that the Prophet forged the Quran. Nothing to confuse or ponder.

tree:0p6o0qa0j84qt2.why: The rarer order of the two names (Wise before Knowing) closes both ayat, after 'and He is' in 43:84 and 'indeed He is' in 51:30. Useful for a memorizer who expects the usual order.

tree:09hxjed0rtg9e3.why: This name of God occurs only in these two ayat, after 'your Lord is' (15:86) and 'yes, and He is' (36:81). Both tie God's creating to His power to raise and judge.
tree:09hxjed0rtg9e3.relation: The Creator who knows all can surely create again.

tree:1o5n4to0ozk52w.why: Both remind people that God brought them into being: from one soul (6:98) and with hearing, sight and hearts (67:23). Same opening, different blessing named.
tree:1o5n4to0ozk52w.relation: God's creating of man as a call to understand (6:98) and to give thanks (67:23).

tree:17syjqw1m30mt4.why: God sends down rain after despair (42:28) and sends down clear signs to bring people out of darkness (57:9). Rain and revelation side by side is a classic thought to ponder.
tree:17syjqw1m30mt4.relation: Similarity: rain revives the land, revelation revives hearts; both are His mercy.

tree:0a9sa050iy56ax.why: Both are declarations of God's oneness closing on the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. 2:163 states it plainly; 59:22 adds knowledge of the unseen and the seen.

30:5|44:42.why: Both close a mention of God's help or mercy with the same pair of names, after 'and He is' (30:5) and 'indeed He is' (44:42). The phrase is common, but here the lead-in fits the closing in both.
30:5|44:42.relation: God's help for whom He wills and His mercy on whom He has mercy, both from the Mighty, the Merciful.

tree:1j98weh0qg5zsd.why: The closing 'and He is the Most High, the Most Great' occurs only here, and in both it follows 'to Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth'. A clear mutashabih between the Throne Verse and 42:4.

tree:1mtup5v1b2z5wj.why: Same pair of names closing two ayat, after 'your Lord is' in 11:66 (saving Salih) and 'and He is' in 42:19 (provision). The lead-in is what a memorizer must keep apart.

tree:01qoaxj1hdkwir.why: The only two ayat ending 'and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware', both about God's knowledge: He perceives all sight (6:103), He knows what He created (67:14).
tree:01qoaxj1hdkwir.relation: The names fit the point: nothing escapes the One who is subtle and aware.

tree:0d6m2vz1mkak25.why: Both end 'and He is the best of providers' in a talk about wealth: the Prophet asks no payment, his Lord's reward is better (23:72); what you spend He replaces (34:39).
tree:0d6m2vz1mkak25.relation: Provision from God is better than what people give or keep.

tree:1xcascl05yqg93.why: Only the stock phrase 'it is better for him' is shared. Voluntary extra fasting (2:184) and honouring God's sanctities on the pilgrimage (22:30) are different subjects, and nothing more links them.

tree:0e8ca551x5w3dx.why: Both are about speech: debate in the best way (16:125) and say what is best (17:53). The same words are followed by a different reason (your Lord knows / Satan sows discord).
tree:0e8ca551x5w3dx.relation: The best words: in calling others to God and among believers, against Satan's discord.

tree:1tkzglh066esxn.why: The faces of the disbelievers in two moments: now they show rejection when the ayat are recited (22:72); on the Day they darken when they see what they denied (67:27).
tree:1tkzglh066esxn.relation: Contrast: the face shows hostility in this world and grief in the next.

tree:1xcvsap0x3am13.why: Both describe the wrongdoers' faces in the Fire: thrown face-first (27:90), turned over while they wish they had obeyed (33:66). Same scene from two sides.

tree:0duhivo09wkfzi.why: The only two places with 'they wish you would disbelieve', both warning against taking enemies as allies. Same theme, different position in the ayah (opening vs ending).
tree:0duhivo09wkfzi.relation: The enemy's true wish is your disbelief, so do not take them as protectors.

tree:1b8t4wg1kw60mo.why: God's mercy embraces everything: God says it (7:156), and the angels pray with it (40:7), adding knowledge. A beautiful pair to ponder.
tree:1b8t4wg1kw60mo.relation: God's word about His mercy and the angels' prayer that answers it.

tree:09mftyq0tgjjda.why: Two ayat of one passage on the end of time in an-Naml: when the word falls due, the Beast comes out (27:82); the word falls due and they cannot speak (27:85). A pair a memorizer must keep in order.
tree:09mftyq0tgjjda.relation: The same decree, first as a sign before the Hour, then as the silencing of the wrongdoers.

tree:0yfxc8r0lxndcz.why: The only two descriptions of the Fire whose fuel is people and stones: prepared for the disbelievers (2:24), and a warning to believers to guard themselves and their families (66:6).
tree:0yfxc8r0lxndcz.relation: The same Fire threatens the deniers and is a reason for believers to protect their homes.

tree:149uwip15lgln3.why: Unlawful gain is fire in the belly, said twice: of those who hide the Book for a small price (2:174) and of those who eat the orphan's wealth (4:10). Rare image, close wording.
tree:149uwip15lgln3.relation: Similarity: both sell a trust for money, and both eat fire.

tree:0iwzxsq1lh1cna.why: Both address the people of understanding and then end differently: 'that you may be mindful' (2:179) and 'that you may succeed' (5:100). A clean memorizer's trap.

tree:07xrutt0kuywyh.why: Only the common call 'O people, only ...' is shared. One ayah is about people who rebel after being saved at sea (10:23), the other the Prophet stating he is a warner (22:49). Different subjects, nothing to learn.

tree:1ww1eiq15nqdmu.why: Both are about enemies stretching out their hands against the believers: God held them back (5:11), and they would do it if they could (60:2).
tree:1ww1eiq15nqdmu.relation: God's past protection (5:11) and the standing danger from enemies (60:2).

tree:1b6h7j30q26o71.why: Two neighbouring ayat about desert Arabs, one counts what he spends as a loss, the other as a way to draw near to God. Same words, opposite intention.
tree:1b6h7j30q26o71.relation: Contrast: the same spending is a burden to one and a means of nearness to another.

tree:0stegkx1v44z03.why: God completing His favour on a chosen servant: Joseph and Jacob's family (12:6) and the Prophet Muhammad (48:2). Same promise to two prophets.
tree:0stegkx1v44z03.relation: Similarity: the favour completed on Joseph and on Muhammad, both after hardship.

tree:06hjuw80kp436m.why: Only the common phrase 'and God turns in mercy to' is shared. 9:15 is about fighting the oath-breakers, 33:73 about the trust carried by man. The lead-ins and closings differ, so a reciter is unlikely to mix them.

tree:19elbjw0gs059a.why: The only two places with 'and they think they are rightly guided', both about people who take devils as allies or companions (7:30, 43:36-37).
tree:19elbjw0gs059a.relation: Following devils while thinking oneself guided: the worst kind of misguidance.

tree:0t3mdql1dgm06h.why: God establishing the truth by His words: at Badr, cutting off the disbelievers (8:7), and against the claim that the Prophet forged the Quran (42:24).
tree:0t3mdql1dgm06h.relation: God makes the truth stand by His words, in battle and in revelation.

tree:1x6gjxf10r8v6j.why: Two images of the dead coming out of the graves: like scattered locusts (54:7) and rushing as if to a target (70:43). Same scene, different simile.
tree:1x6gjxf10r8v6j.relation: The Resurrection scene drawn with two similes.

tree:0t1q79p0ic728p.why: Nothing is hidden from God: Abraham says it in prayer (14:38), and it is shown on the Day when all come out before Him (40:16). Negation differs, which a memorizer must note.

tree:0lv02tn19511rt.why: God does not break His promise: said to those hastening the punishment (22:47) and about the Romans' coming victory (30:6). 'Will never' vs 'does not' is the trap.
tree:0lv02tn19511rt.relation: God's promise holds, whether of punishment or of victory.

tree:0e2yfie0jsz3da.why: Both describe the patient believers who repel evil with good and spend from what they are given, in a different order and with a different reward named.
tree:0e2yfie0jsz3da.relation: The same character praised in two places: patience, repelling evil with good, spending.

tree:1rn0fba11o3bya.why: Two neighbouring ayat: on the Day they are called to prostrate and cannot (68:42), because in the world they were called while healthy and refused (68:43).
tree:1rn0fba11o3bya.relation: Contrast: the call refused in health becomes the call they cannot answer.

tree:1w1acct13pkkzr.why: Those who call to the Fire: idolaters one might marry (2:221) and Pharaoh's leaders (28:41). 2:221 contrasts it with God calling to the Garden.
tree:1w1acct13pkkzr.relation: Contrast: who invites to the Fire and who invites to Paradise.

tree:0q0skmm1sdpbd6.why: Houses of God and the remembrance of His name: the worst wrongdoer prevents it (2:114); in houses God allowed to be raised it is done morning and evening (24:36).
tree:0q0skmm1sdpbd6.relation: Contrast: blocking the mosques vs filling them with remembrance.

tree:0ck2kmb1ihd6zj.why: Both are about God's will in guidance: He did not will to purify some hearts (5:41); whom He wills to guide, He opens his chest (6:125). The words are common but the theme is the same.
tree:0ck2kmb1ihd6zj.relation: God's will behind a heart's purity or openness to Islam.

17:68|67:17.why: The same warning: do you feel safe that He will not send a storm of stones on you? 'Do you then feel safe' (17:68) vs 'or do you feel safe' (67:17), and what follows differs.

tree:1146qvq00gl73u.why: Both invite people to look at creation: the shadows bowing (16:48) and the sky and earth around them (34:9). The opening differs ('have they not' with and/so).

tree:030ilgs1qwndgu.why: Two reminders of blessings made for people: night for rest and day for sight (27:86), a safe sanctuary (29:67). The opening differs by one letter.
tree:030ilgs1qwndgu.relation: Signs of mercy that should lead to faith, yet they deny.

tree:1dtnbfu1b4iqh2.why: What Satan wants: to lead far astray through seeking judgment from false authorities (4:60), and to sow enmity through wine and gambling (5:91).
tree:1dtnbfu1b4iqh2.relation: Satan's aims named plainly in two places.

tree:0agzlh80mqdj32.why: God will replace you with another people: if you do not go out to fight (9:39), if you turn away from spending (47:38). Same threat, two duties.
tree:0agzlh80mqdj32.relation: God does not need us; turning away from His cause means being replaced.

tree:07k1ff20vl7z9m.why: Both close a parable with 'thus God sets forth parables': the foam and the water (13:17) and the good tree (14:25). Neighbouring surahs, close wording.
tree:07k1ff20vl7z9m.relation: Two parables of truth that lasts: what benefits stays, the good tree gives fruit.

tree:17nu8k4027hozw.why: The words match but the structure does not: 2:102 says the sorcery they learn does harm them and does not benefit, 10:18 says the idols neither harm nor benefit. Under the card rules that is a different phrase, and the subjects (magic, idol worship) differ too.

tree:1hx46p50iq2tzx.why: Both threaten a painful punishment to those who hang back from fighting in God's cause: the believers at Tabuk (9:39) and the Bedouin who stayed behind (48:16).
tree:1hx46p50iq2tzx.relation: Same warning against holding back when called to go out.

tree:1mxv0ql14i9z03.why: Only the short clause 'and pardons much' is shared, with different subjects: the Prophet passing over much that the People of the Book hid (5:15), and God pardoning sins behind misfortunes (42:30). A rare phrase alone with different subjects is not enough.

tree:0gwk7ol0lbfc1r.why: Only the stock closing 'He knows what you do' is shared, with different lead-ins. Keeping oaths (16:91) and God accepting repentance (42:25) are different subjects.

tree:0yrwzpy07xltas.why: Only 'they know that God' is shared. Hypocrites who forget that God knows what they hide (2:77) and the slanderers who will know on the Day that God is the clear Truth (24:25) are different subjects.

tree:1uftfc21rbreh2.why: The only two places where God covers the day with the night, each in a passage listing signs of creation (the heavens and Throne in 7:54, the earth and its fruits in 13:3).
tree:1uftfc21rbreh2.relation: Night and day as a sign of the Creator's ordering.

tree:0ckk3tt0vq96ld.why: Forgiving those who wronged you: Joseph forgives his brothers (12:92), and the believers are told to forgive a relative who slandered (24:22), with 'do you not love that God forgive you?'
tree:0ckk3tt0vq96ld.relation: Similarity: a wronged man's forgiveness of kin, and the hope of God's forgiveness that should move us to it.

tree:077hb2w055vnhs.why: The only two ayat ending 'and they do what they are commanded', both about angels: those who fear their Lord above them (16:50) and the stern keepers of the Fire (66:6).
tree:077hb2w055vnhs.relation: Angels' complete obedience, as worshippers and as guards of the Fire.

tree:1jpuse90nbr081.why: Only 'they have no power over anything' is shared. The showy spender losing his reward (2:264) and the People of the Book having no control of God's grace (57:29) are different subjects.

tree:0gag7nx0qscvyn.why: The same question on the Day of Judgement, 'what answer were you given / did you give?', put to the messengers (5:109) and to the people they were sent to (28:65).
tree:0gag7nx0qscvyn.relation: Both sides of the message are questioned: the senders and the receivers.

tree:1vzgj3w1ryuqh8.why: Two cries of regret: the owner of the ruined garden wishing he had not associated (18:42), and the one given his book in his left hand (69:25). Same words, the world and the Hereafter.
tree:1vzgj3w1ryuqh8.relation: Regret too late, in this life and in the next.

tree:0uk332u0x0371k.why: Believers saying 'our Lord, we believe' and then asking: to be written with the witnesses (5:83), for forgiveness and mercy (23:109). Same opening, different request.

tree:1ysh7cy1788iog.why: Two neighbouring ayat on divorce, both turning on whether the couple can keep within God's limits. A memorizer must keep apart the wording and endings of each.

tree:0xxxygf1vt9wkf.why: Two calls to the believers, to be mindful of God (8:29) and to repent sincerely (66:8), both promising that He will remove their bad deeds, then a different reward.
tree:0xxxygf1vt9wkf.relation: Taqwa and repentance both wipe away sins.

tree:1wsy4wr1p0kdx9.why: Neighbouring surahs, same promise in the singular: whoever believes and does good (64:9) or whoever is mindful of God (65:5) has his sins removed, then the reward differs.

tree:0fyvpy61bqzmag.why: Only the common phrase 'it is not for us to' is shared. Shu'ayb refusing to return to his people's religion (7:89) and the believers told how to answer the slander (24:16) are different subjects.

tree:0fk2x2a180rbey.why: Both deny that God has a son: glory be to Him (4:171) and how could He when He has no consort (6:101).
tree:0fk2x2a180rbey.relation: The same denial argued two ways: transcendence and creation.

tree:1mw42hv15vlw09.why: Two prophets disowning any authority over revelation in the same words: Jesus never said what he had no right to (5:116), Muhammad cannot change the Quran of his own accord (10:15).
tree:1mw42hv15vlw09.relation: Similarity: a messenger only conveys; he does not add or alter.

tree:16qmkb31fhspnv.why: Same surah, same closing that differs in its last word: 'what they used to do' with two different verbs (6:108, 6:159). A classic memorizer's trap.

tree:1yycytr1njvhun.why: Only 'be sent down on you from' is shared. The envy of those who disbelieve (2:105) and the rain at Badr (8:11) are unrelated subjects.

tree:19z3yw60lpqee8.why: Both are signs of the sky with lightning: He sends down hail from mountains of cloud (24:43) and water that revives the earth (30:24).
tree:19z3yw60lpqee8.relation: From the same sky come harm and mercy, fear and hope.

tree:0n3j1do00bg3zi.why: Turning back on one's heels, both as a test of following the Messenger: the change of qibla (2:143) and the rumour of his death at Uhud (3:144).
tree:0n3j1do00bg3zi.relation: Tests that show who truly follows the Messenger.

tree:1dxj4qt171oc6l.why: Who guides to the truth: God, not the partners (10:35), and the Book the jinn heard (46:30).
tree:1dxj4qt171oc6l.relation: God guides to the truth, and so does His Book.

tree:1efd0us02xe9bk.why: Only 'the Day of Resurrection, then' is shared, a common time phrase. Jesus raised up (3:55) and the one who defrauds (3:161) are different subjects.

tree:14y8m231k2kl3n.why: Only 'the Day of Resurrection, what' is shared, and the 'what' is a different word in each (a negation in 5:36, a relative pronoun in 16:92).

tree:1vca0xi1js8lce.why: The same mocking objection of the deniers: that the reminder was sent down to this man. 15:6 says it as a taunt of madness, 38:8 as a jealous question, which a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1vca0xi1js8lce.relation: The same objection from Quraysh in two surahs, once as mockery and once as envy.

tree:0ef85u308qv6sf.why: A rare clause, whoever disbelieves bears his own disbelief, then two different continuations: 30:44 turns to those who do good, 35:39 says disbelief only adds to the deniers' loss. A clear memorizer pair.
tree:0ef85u308qv6sf.relation: Each person carries his own disbelief; one surah sets the doers of good beside it, the other the growing loss of the deniers.

tree:0gv6sax0y1wml9.why: The shared words are a different structure: in 9:128 the Prophet is grieved by what burdens you, in 24:54 he bears only what he was charged with. Different subjects, nothing to learn together.

tree:1ocsqn00e42w6e.why: Only a pronoun and a negation meet by accident: patience with prayer in 20:132, the natural disposition in 30:30. No shared phrase or theme.

tree:14bof9z1h4dx1d.why: Two unrelated uses: the disciples wish to be witnesses to the table in 5:113, and no creature would be left on earth in 16:61. Nothing in common.

tree:0g9xitx07etq17.why: A rare expression, the life grew long for them, used both times of past generations whom time made heedless. 21:44 has one verb form, 28:45 the stronger form, an easy slip.
tree:0g9xitx07etq17.relation: Long life and long time made earlier generations forget; both ayat explain heedlessness by the passing of time.

tree:0fp6tbf05dyv3t.why: In 4:91 authority is given to the believers over hostile people; in 30:35 it is a denied proof sent down to idolaters. Different subjects and meanings.

tree:0d69lfc1hypz7o.why: Both ayat are about Jesus as a witness over his people: 4:159 on the Day of Resurrection, 5:117 in his own words while he lived among them. The row for 4:159 reads on into 4:160, which has nothing to do with the match.
tree:0d69lfc1hypz7o.relation: Jesus as witness over the People of the Book, foretold in one surah and spoken by him in the other.

tree:1th2bfo0jxfpli.why: Two kinds of deniers, the apostate and those who dispute about God after He was answered, receive the same sentence of anger and punishment, ending in different adjectives. Good for memorizers and for pondering.
tree:1th2bfo0jxfpli.relation: Apostasy and false dispute about God earn the same wrath.

tree:16mfehy1bxce24.why: Both end on the question of who is a guardian over people: no one will plead for traitors before God (4:109), and the Prophet was not sent as their guardian (17:54). A memorizer ending pair; both rows read on into the next ayah only because of the run-on.

tree:0cpxc8l1ccw5y5.why: Only a pronoun and a conjunction meet: regrets of the followers in the Fire (2:167) and God guarding the idolaters (42:6). Different subjects.

tree:051gq051p6qz2t.why: Two separate rulings in one surah, waiting period after divorce and the outer garment, joined only by a preposition. Nothing to learn together.

tree:1ya3k0t1j3r22f.why: A stock phrase about what they say: a threat to the Trinitarians in 5:73 and a glorification formula in 17:43. Different frames, no slip and no shared theme.

tree:0jldeh40tfff7w.why: Two peoples accuse their messenger of turning them from their gods: Quraysh in 25:42 and the people of Hud in 46:22. The same complaint recurs across generations.
tree:0jldeh40tfff7w.relation: Different peoples answer their prophets with the same complaint about their gods.

50:17|70:37.why: A rare paired expression, from the right and from the left, used of the recording angels in 50:17 and of the deniers crowding around the Prophet in 70:37. Easy to confuse in recitation.
50:17|70:37.relation: The same words describe the angels sitting to record and the deniers sitting in groups around the Prophet.

tree:0x4vgco1dz1rco.why: A rare phrase about desire: the Prophet does not speak from desire (53:3), and the one who fears his Lord holds his soul back from desire (79:40). Worth pondering together. Both rows read on into the next ayah, which completes each thought.
tree:0x4vgco1dz1rco.relation: Freedom from desire: the Prophet is free of it, and the believer earns paradise by restraining it.

tree:02di7xe1uevs18.why: A preposition and a noun meet by chance: a warning about being lured from part of the revelation (5:49) and the Prophet passing over part of a secret (66:3). Unrelated.

tree:1fgljac15oxik8.why: A rare phrase, by mutual consent, governs two dealings: weaning by both parents (2:233) and trade between believers (4:29). The pronoun differs, an easy slip.
tree:1fgljac15oxik8.relation: Mutual consent as the condition of lawful dealings, in family matters and in trade.

tree:0rsbqfh083xz39.why: Both describe the one who turned away from God's remembrance and wants only this world, and the Prophet is told how to treat him. Same theme, wording close enough to confuse.
tree:0rsbqfh083xz39.relation: Heedlessness of God's remembrance goes with wanting the life of this world.

tree:0c9gzqr1m0kzl3.why: Both are about turning from God's remembrance and the blindness that follows: eyes veiled from it in this life (18:101), raised blind on the Day of Resurrection (20:124). A real theme for pondering.
tree:0c9gzqr1m0kzl3.relation: Blindness to God's remembrance in this world becomes blindness on the Day of Resurrection.

tree:1b5etzb0ur2xr7.why: Different structures: God turns the hail away from whom He wills (24:43), and the Prophet turns away from whoever turned away (53:29). Nothing shared in meaning.

tree:0tamjur1gss223.why: Both challenge idolaters to produce evidence for their claims about God, once knowledge (6:148), once authority (10:68). Same argument, the noun differs.
tree:0tamjur1gss223.relation: The deniers are asked for proof and have none, whether they speak of God's will or of a son.

tree:0toylqb0owmi89.why: Intercession with God only by His permission, in the Throne verse and in 34:23, both ending with two of His names. Same doctrine, slightly different wording.
tree:0toylqb0owmi89.relation: No one intercedes with God except by His leave.

tree:0i6fi311ureyff.why: Hiding a testimony one holds from God (2:140) and no favour owed to anyone (92:19) share only a preposition. Unrelated.

tree:0dc1frz0mhozdj.why: False gods cannot remove harm from you (17:56) and God is free of need of you (39:7): the shared words are a different structure, subjects differ.

92:11|111:2.why: The same clause, his wealth will not avail him, said of the miser in 92:11 and of Abu Lahab in 111:2, once as a future question and once as a past fact.
92:11|111:2.relation: Wealth cannot save the one who denies, whether a type of person or a named enemy.

tree:11z5kvw0n9e804.why: Only a turning away and a saying meet: believers turning from idle talk (28:55) and deniers turning from the Prophet (44:14). A stock frame, different subjects.

tree:1fcpy201vsb862.why: Yaqub's precaution could not avail his sons (12:68) and the punishment of Hell is not lightened (35:36). The shared words are only a pronoun and a preposition.

tree:1rrxw8e0vz5c2c.why: Pleading for someone on the Day of Resurrection (4:109) and turning away from deniers (54:6): the shared words are a different structure each time.

tree:05cm8ra07cfsqm.why: What was hidden from Adam and his wife (7:20) and two prophets unable to avail their wives (66:10): a pronoun and a preposition, nothing more.

tree:0tq8rfg0jhhyf0.why: A rare phrase, We made a covenant with, opens God's charge to Ibrahim and to Adam. Ibrahim and Ismail were charged to purify the House; Adam forgot and had no resolve.
tree:0tq8rfg0jhhyf0.relation: Two covenants: one kept by Ibrahim and Ismail, one forgotten by Adam.

tree:1l9e3x41rwmi26.why: Same surah, same battle: the hypocrites had pledged to God not to turn their backs (33:15), while true believers kept what they pledged (33:23).
tree:1l9e3x41rwmi26.relation: Contrast: those who broke their pledge to God and those who were true to it.

tree:1q7fhzf0443atp.why: Both close a promise of increased reward to believers with the same pair of names, Forgiving and Appreciative, in two neighbouring surahs: one with a pronoun, one with God's name. A memorizer pair. Both rows read on into the next ayah, which adds nothing to the match.
tree:1q7fhzf0443atp.relation: God gives more than the deed deserves, which is why He is called Forgiving and Appreciative.

tree:0s108f815f9rg8.why: Two unrelated rulings, those excused by disability from fighting (4:95) and male attendants without desire (24:31), sharing a two-word particle phrase. Different subjects, little slip risk.

tree:1b8x9t50hgm089.why: The hoopoe stayed not long (27:22) and Paradise is brought near, not far (50:31). The same adverb, unrelated scenes.

tree:1xuaxd80t3ry5i.why: A barren valley at the House (14:37) and a Quran without crookedness (39:28) share only a negating construction. Different subjects, nothing to ponder together.

tree:0sbbufp1yad683.why: Al-Fath twice promises a near victory: as reward for the pledge under the tree (48:18) and as what came before the fulfilled dream (48:27). Same ending in one surah, easy to confuse. The run-on rows add the next ayah, which the match does not need.
tree:0sbbufp1yad683.relation: The pledge and the dream both lead to the same near victory.

tree:0olgmwu1qj2rg2.why: Deniers rejoice in what they have, the blessings opened to them (6:44) or their own knowledge (40:83), and then the punishment seizes them. Same pattern of false security.
tree:0olgmwu1qj2rg2.relation: Rejoicing in what one has, instead of in the message, comes just before the seizing.

tree:0w0y6uo0zsnpfs.why: People rejoice in a good wind or a mercy, then fall into panic or despair when it changes (10:22, 30:36). Same picture of human fickleness.
tree:0w0y6uo0zsnpfs.relation: Joy in a passing mercy turns to fear or despair the moment it is taken.

tree:13362fs0z20n8a.why: Both reassure the Prophet about a household matter in which God has given him room: his marriage that God ordained (33:38) and the release from his oath (66:2).
tree:13362fs0z20n8a.relation: What God has allowed for the Prophet is no fault, and he should not deny himself it.

tree:1kr3zw01p6hkoe.why: Pharaoh sends heralds to the cities (26:53) and calls out to his people about his kingdom (43:51): different moments and verbs, only his name and a preposition shared.

tree:1xowucf08kyv3j.why: The destruction of what Pharaoh and his people built (7:137) and the signs sent to them (27:12): only the name of the people is shared, not a phrase or a point.

tree:05capuk1c3hojo.why: Pharaoh's command was not right-guided (11:97) and Pharaoh's question about the Lord of the worlds (26:23): the conjunction is a different structure each time.

tree:1a42d9o08lc1v4.why: A party of the People of the Book who threw away the Book (2:101) and a party of God's servants who prayed (23:109): the same generic noun, opposite subjects without a shared point.

tree:0a0oi8m1mpydxa.why: A rare phrase, a party you kill, used of the Israelites who killed prophets (2:87) and of the believers' victory over the People of the Book at the Trench (33:26). Easy to confuse. The row for 2:87 reads on into 2:88, which the match does not need.
tree:0a0oi8m1mpydxa.relation: Those who once killed a party of the prophets later saw a party of their own killed.

tree:10mufh41j92yk0.why: In one surah: its ayat are set out clearly as an Arabic Quran (41:3), and had it been foreign they would have asked why its ayat were not set out (41:44). The second answers the first.
tree:10mufh41j92yk0.relation: The Arabic Quran with clear ayat, and the excuse the deniers would have made without it.

tree:114kr6b0kdi7v1.why: God's favour over others: over all the worlds for the prophets in 6:86, and over many believers for Dawud and Sulayman in 27:15, who thank God for it. A memorizer pair.
tree:114kr6b0kdi7v1.relation: Favour is given to prophets; Dawud and Sulayman answer it with praise.

tree:08nank912nxtwt.why: Arguing about Ibrahim (3:65) and the good example in Ibrahim (60:4) share only his name after a preposition. Different subjects and frames.

tree:15tswn11mtz8wh.why: Among the people of the Garden (46:16) and among the people of the Blaze (67:10): a generic phrase with different subjects, not a real contrast between the two ayat.

tree:01p31yk1r2gv74.why: Iron collars on the deniers' necks, in this life as a picture of their blindness (36:8) and in the Fire as they are dragged (40:71). Same image, different word order.
tree:01p31yk1r2gv74.relation: The collars that keep the deniers from seeing the truth are the collars of their punishment.

25:7|25:20.why: In one surah, the deniers object that the messenger eats food and walks in the markets (25:7), and God answers that every messenger before him did the same (25:20).
25:7|25:20.relation: Objection and answer in the same words.

tree:0o75cwa1ntrezk.why: People of the Book who think they owe nothing to the unlettered (3:75) and the messenger raised among the unlettered (62:2) share a rare word but no point or subject.

tree:0lcow1c1nz7nxm.why: Neighbouring hajj rulings, fasting during hajj and no dispute during hajj, sharing only the word for hajj. Not a mutashabih and not a relation.

tree:16lbdol0t108ub.why: Freeing slaves appears in two lists of where wealth goes: righteousness (2:177) and the recipients of charity (9:60). Two long lists a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:16lbdol0t108ub.relation: The ransoming of slaves is part of both voluntary righteousness and obligatory charity.

tree:191cufb14zwvhj.why: Al-Qamar ends two ayat in the scriptures: the deniers have no exemption written there (54:43), and all they did is written there (54:52). The runs read on, and 54:53 completes the second.
tree:191cufb14zwvhj.relation: No exemption is written for the deniers, but every deed of theirs is.

tree:0vrzkac1k3jfm0.why: The hypocrites find fault in the matter of charity: with the Prophet's share-out (9:58) and with poor believers who give their little (9:79). Same surah, same theme.
tree:0vrzkac1k3jfm0.relation: Faultfinding about charity marks the hypocrites, whoever is the target.

tree:1jgj40f00x565f.why: Mentioning God alone in the Quran (17:46) and the cursed tree in the Quran (17:60) share only the word. Different subjects.

tree:0as57pk0pfe6ja.why: Walking among people with light (6:122) and the call to hajj among people (22:27): only a preposition and a noun.

tree:1hqzddg031cbew.why: Musa asks for a partner in his task (20:32) and the queen asks for counsel in her affair (27:32): different stories, only a common noun with a pronoun.

tree:01aximg1ahcp0a.why: People surging into one another (18:99) and obeying in part of the matter (47:26): unrelated.

tree:1y4cugs09icyae.why: What you store in your houses (3:49) and had you stayed in your houses (3:154): different stories, the shared words carry no point.

tree:029hvbs1m8q8gc.why: Two consecutive commands to the Prophet's wives about their houses: stay in them, and remember what is recited in them. A memorizer pair that also shows the house as a place of revelation.
tree:029hvbs1m8q8gc.relation: The wives' homes are where they stay and where revelation is recited.

tree:12vvrmb04khvep.why: Two promises to the believers in the same shape, as for those who..., then in God's mercy (3:107, 4:175). Near in wording and meaning.
tree:12vvrmb04khvep.relation: The believers' end is God's mercy, in both surahs.

tree:18vetkj0abf249.why: God speaks of those harmed in His way (3:195) and of going out to strive in His way (60:1), but the ayat are about reward and about secret friendship with enemies. Only a phrase in passing is shared.

tree:0lpbqsd1iega59.why: Whatever affair you are engaged in (10:61) and every day He is about some matter (55:29): the same noun in two different senses and subjects.

tree:10chfhi11agzym.why: Those who turn away are in dissension (2:137) and who is more astray than one in far dissension (41:52): a stock description of deniers, different addressees and arguments.

53:36|80:13.why: The scrolls of Musa (53:36) and the honoured scrolls of the Quran (80:13) share only one noun. Different subjects.

tree:0qki3xo0xz9l70.why: The people of Paradise in shades, reclining on couches (36:56) or with springs (77:41). Same picture, different completion: a memorizer pair.
tree:0qki3xo0xz9l70.relation: Shade and rest as the reward of the God-fearing.

tree:16ow82y1rgi7mw.why: In neighbouring surahs, the wrongdoers are in lasting punishment (42:45) and the criminals in the punishment of Hell forever (43:74). Close wording, easy to swap.
tree:16ow82y1rgi7mw.relation: Wrongdoing and crime end in the same abiding punishment.

tree:1h1ye77011kppr.why: Deniers are drowned in heedlessness: their hearts in a flood of it (23:63), themselves heedless in it (51:11). A rare word used the same way.
tree:1h1ye77011kppr.relation: Heedlessness pictured as a flood that covers the heart.

tree:10wcpnk1odpfqi.why: What is in the hypocrite's heart (2:204) and one with disease in his heart (33:32): different people and points, only a common phrase.

tree:1913sx50ix389b.why: Yusuf kept the accusation to himself (12:77) and Musa felt fear within himself (20:67). Different verbs and moments, only the phrase within himself is shared.

tree:0rhqzk216a1obw.why: A mark on the believers' faces: the trace of prostration in this life (48:29) and the radiance of bliss in the next (83:24). A worthwhile pairing for pondering.
tree:0rhqzk216a1obw.relation: The mark of prostration in this world becomes the radiance of bliss in Paradise.

tree:1ldwpou15u3tsk.why: Signs in Yusuf and his brothers (12:7) and how you failed with Yusuf (12:80): his name after a preposition, two different points.

tree:0vdcul61d4p1oa.why: Two descriptions of hypocrites in battle: had they gone out among you they would have added only trouble (9:47), had they been among you they would have fought little (33:20). Same structure and theme.
tree:0vdcul61d4p1oa.relation: The hypocrites' presence in the army would have helped nothing.

tree:1hjyplv0oq0bg1.why: Never stand in that mosque (9:108) and abiding in it forever (18:3): the same adverb, unrelated subjects.

tree:04czkal0k6bu4n.why: The same parable in two surahs: no master would share his provision with his slaves as an equal, so how do they give God partners. Wording differs in pronoun and frame.
tree:04czkal0k6bu4n.relation: Parable against shirk: you would not make your slaves your equals, yet you make God's creatures His.

tree:1xqolzn1gdnt5v.why: Partners in a dead animal (6:139) and a man owned by quarrelling partners (39:29): the same word, different subjects and points.

tree:14n23s211s6fyw.why: The Book with guidance in it: the Quran is guidance for the God-fearing (2:2) and the Injil had guidance and light (5:46), which also ends with the God-fearing.
tree:14n23s211s6fyw.relation: Each revealed book carries guidance for the God-fearing.

tree:15nyiob0tz3y23.why: Disagreement over the Book (2:213) and God witnessing what you do (10:61): only a pronoun and a conjunction meet.

tree:0ho75930zuogzx.why: An ayah ending about what they doubted: the punishment brought to Lut's people (15:63), and Isa, the word of truth (19:34). Different subjects but a shared ending a memorizer can confuse. Both rows read on into the next ayah.

tree:146w4y10msh77b.why: The law of retaliation written in the Torah (5:45) and the arrogant in the Fire (40:48): different particles and structures.

tree:0x5c7js0h2227i.why: The cup of Paradise: passed among them without idle talk (52:23), served mixed with ginger (76:17). Same scene, different completion.
tree:0x5c7js0h2227i.relation: The drink of Paradise, free of sin and fragrant.

tree:14itmts131l7g8.why: No fatigue touches the people of Paradise: said of them (15:48) and said by them in thanks (35:35). Same promise, different person.
tree:14itmts131l7g8.relation: The promise of rest, then the believers voicing it in Paradise.

tree:1vn8in61k8txew.why: Regret over neglect of the Hour (6:31) and full payment in this world (11:15): a pronoun and a conjunction meet by chance.

tree:11hej170ik3vp9.why: Had God known good in them (8:23) and if you know good in your slaves (24:33): the same phrase, entirely different subjects.

tree:15agzqa0largwa.why: Two descriptions of the gardens in ar-Rahman: two springs flowing (55:50) and two springs gushing (55:66). A classic memorizer pair.
tree:15agzqa0largwa.relation: The higher pair of gardens and the lower pair, told apart by their springs.

tree:0i4purg1moypto.why: Enter the Fire with the nations (7:38) and enter Egypt in safety (12:99): a common verb, unrelated scenes.

tree:0sr44nf0rmiaoj.why: Two prophets answer a threat with the same question: Shuayb to the chiefs who threaten exile (7:88), Musa to Pharaoh who threatens prison (26:30).
tree:0sr44nf0rmiaoj.relation: A prophet threatened by the powerful answers: even if?

tree:0ogsrzi09nx2uc.why: Musa's two replies, about the place they sought (18:64) and the agreement with his father-in-law (28:28), share only the opening said, that. No point together.

tree:0im1h130n0rg99.why: Two prophets answer their deniers by leaving the matter to their Lord's knowledge: the Prophet (21:4) and Shuayb (26:188). Short replies easy to confuse.
tree:0im1h130n0rg99.relation: The prophet's answer to denial: my Lord knows.

tree:18dyeat1v8unl9.why: Two prophets begin with glory to You when facing God: Isa disowning what was said of him (5:116), Musa after asking to see God (7:143).
tree:18dyeat1v8unl9.relation: Prophets answer God's majesty by declaring Him free of all fault.

tree:1x6vjju147feeg.why: Musa twice says perhaps my Lord or perhaps your Lord: comforting his people (7:129) and setting out to Madyan alone (28:22). His hope in God, for others and for himself.
tree:1x6vjju147feeg.relation: Musa's hope in his Lord, alone in flight and as leader of his people.

tree:1613sx30iug3cf.why: Two times in the same surah a firm no: God reassures Musa before Pharaoh (26:15), and Musa reassures his people at the sea (26:62).
tree:1613sx30iug3cf.relation: Musa received the reassurance from God, and later gave it to his people with the same word.

tree:0jkwri11mvquy5.why: Ibrahim's fear of going astray (6:77) and Pharaoh's threat of prison (26:29) share only the opening particle. Different structures and subjects.

tree:1a8zq9d06znist.why: You will not see Me (7:143) and I will not send him (12:66): the negation is a common word, the scenes unrelated.

tree:1x4tjwb1d2n67b.why: Lut's wish for strength (11:80) and Musa's remark about payment (18:77): a common conditional particle, nothing in common.

tree:03dzhlf1csmult.why: Who are my helpers (3:52) and who will revive bones (36:78): an interrogative only, unrelated subjects.

tree:0v5hv411ubru6b.why: She seduced me (12:26) and it is my staff (20:18): a pronoun after said, unrelated.

tree:12du92a1ydfcli.why: God's reply about the disbeliever's provision (2:126) and Ibrahim's reply about despair (15:56): the shared opening is a different structure each time.

tree:1yma44u1rvqdc6.why: Two sons address their fathers about a dream: Yusuf when it comes true (12:100), Ismail when told to obey it (37:102). A meaningful pair for pondering.
tree:1yma44u1rvqdc6.relation: Prophetic dreams between father and son: one fulfilled in honour, one accepted in submission.

tree:00zneje0nejbag.why: Adam addressed by name twice: God tells him to inform the angels (2:33), Satan tempts him with the tree (20:120).
tree:00zneje0nejbag.relation: Contrast: God's call to Adam raises him with knowledge, Satan's call deceives him.

tree:0c5e0xx1hfvn47.why: Sulayman addresses two audiences in one surah: the people about the favour given him (27:16), the chiefs about the throne (27:38). A memorizer pair.
tree:0c5e0xx1hfvn47.relation: Sulayman's speech to his people and to his court.

tree:0ehi8pk0k6409u.why: Two wishes: the believing man in Paradise wishes his people knew (36:26), the denier wishes he were far from his companion (43:38). Same opening, opposite ends.
tree:0ehi8pk0k6409u.relation: Contrast: a wish of mercy from Paradise and a wish of regret from the punishment.

tree:1bfh7nu1xwkbcq.why: Two pairs pray together, our Lord: Adam and his wife confessing wrong (7:23), Musa and Harun voicing fear (20:45). Same opening, a memorizer pair.
tree:1bfh7nu1xwkbcq.relation: Two pairs turn to their Lord, one in repentance and one in fear.

tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.why: 2:235 and 2:284 both warn that God knows, and will reckon with, what you hide in yourselves. 51:21 (signs in yourselves) and 57:22 (afflictions) use the phrase for unrelated things.
tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.changes: Removed 51:21 and 57:22: same phrase, unrelated subjects.
tree:1hyf1n319k3wc9.relation: God's knowledge of what is hidden in the self, as a warning in a law of marriage and as a general reckoning.

tree:1kbc6t003oam5m.why: 2:164 and 3:190 open the same way and a memorizer must keep apart the long list in 2:164 from the short one in 3:190. 3:191 and 67:3 carry the same call to look into creation.
tree:1kbc6t003oam5m.relation: Creation as a sign: listed, then reflected on by the people of understanding, then shown to have no flaw.

tree:0qqlksl0bmc77f.why: 2:49, 7:141 and 14:6 tell the rescue from Pharaoh in almost the same words; a memorizer must track the verb that differs in each. 6:99 is the stock closing about signs, a different phrase.
tree:0qqlksl0bmc77f.changes: Removed 6:99: its words are a different phrase (signs for believers), not the trial from your Lord.

tree:1khadwg043i6ja.why: 3:29 and 3:154 both speak of what is in your chests as known and tested by God. 17:51 and 40:80 use the phrase for something unrelated (a hard substance, a need).
tree:1khadwg043i6ja.changes: Removed 17:51 and 40:80: same phrase, unrelated meaning.
tree:1khadwg043i6ja.relation: What is hidden in the chest is known to God and brought out by trial.

tree:19pkro31ojd2l7.why: All four are about heedlessness before the Hour: two describe people heedless now, two have them confess on the Day that they were heedless.
tree:19pkro31ojd2l7.relation: Heedless in this life, then the confession on the Day when the cover is lifted.

tree:1rpenay0pme6zk.why: All four are about the benefits God put in cattle; a memorizer must tell apart how each one continues.
tree:1rpenay0pme6zk.relation: The favour of cattle, each time joined to a different lesson: the sacrifice, the drink, thanks, and travel.

tree:01dqdc919ilz8p.why: Only a speech opener with a conditional is shared; the speakers and subjects are unrelated (Pharaoh, Noah, Moses, a denier).

tree:0qxg2j51b5c9qf.why: 15:57 and 51:31 are Ibrahim's identical question to the angels, and 20:95 is Moses asking the Samiri in the same form; 20:51 is Pharaoh's question in the same surah. Useful for a memorizer keeping these questions apart.

tree:1jhhjif0mcvgnz.why: A set of the sayings the Quran reports from the Jews, each answered; worth seeing together.
tree:1jhhjif0mcvgnz.relation: The claims of the People of the Book, one after another, and how each is refuted.

tree:1bph3e91gpmirj.why: Four women addressing their Lord: the mother of Maryam, Maryam, the Queen of Sheba and the wife of Pharaoh.
tree:1bph3e91gpmirj.relation: Women's prayers in the Quran: a vow, wonder at a promise, repentance, and a plea for a house in Paradise.

tree:0ajr3em06590bs.why: The deniers' question about being raised after turning to bones and dust, repeated with small differences a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:0ajr3em06590bs.relation: The same denial of resurrection and the answers given to it.

tree:089wtfu0cz7nm8.why: Peoples answering their prophets with the same question (Hud twice, Moses and Ibrahim); 7:70 and 46:22 even end the same way.
tree:089wtfu0cz7nm8.relation: Different prophets, the same rejection: you came to turn us from what our fathers worshipped.

tree:1pow2rw1uuiwte.why: 11:69, 15:52 and 51:25 are the angels greeting Ibrahim, each with a different reply; a classic set for memorizers. 25:63 is the servants of the Merciful answering the ignorant, another subject.
tree:1pow2rw1uuiwte.changes: Removed 25:63 (with 25:64): a different scene and meaning.

tree:1vin96l098p9hb.why: 26:116 and 26:167 are the threats to Noah and to Lot in the same mould; 7:149 and 12:14 share the opening and the losers ending. Good for a memorizer.
