tree:0nf8oxt02h8jdt.why: The cry of woe of those who see the punishment or the resurrection, each followed by a different confession.
tree:0nf8oxt02h8jdt.relation: Confessions at the moment of truth: we were wrongdoers, we were transgressors, this is the Day of Judgement.

tree:1cex98g1ctkpgq.why: Only a time phrase is shared; the subjects are unrelated (news of the unseen, Salih's people, Maryam in labour, a challenge to idolaters).

tree:1v7h4ty1dlundw.why: What true success is: the believers, the one who purifies himself, while Pharaoh's magicians claim success goes to whoever dominates today.
tree:1v7h4ty1dlundw.relation: Contrast: the magicians' worldly idea of success against the success of purification and faith.

tree:0s22xu312yui61.why: 6:31 and 10:45 are the same sentence about those who deny meeting God; 6:140 and 4:119 name others who lost. Useful for a memorizer.
tree:0s22xu312yui61.relation: Who the losers are: deniers of the meeting with God, killers of their children, followers of Satan.

tree:0c9x5a20ji88ky.why: A common phrase about going astray, said of different groups in unrelated contexts; nothing to learn from the grouping.

tree:1k11fsb18arc3h.why: The Quran described as an Arabic Quran, each time with a different purpose; 20:113 and 42:7 open the same way, which a memorizer must keep apart.
tree:1k11fsb18arc3h.relation: Why the Quran came in Arabic: so they may be mindful, so people who know understand, to warn the mother of towns.

tree:1q5lh4v1sv9kyb.why: Towns God destroyed, each mention adding something: the sudden punishment, their not believing, their not returning, their ruins.
tree:1q5lh4v1sv9kyb.relation: The destroyed towns as a lesson, seen from four sides.

tree:0ftuney0pnblw8.why: 17:56 and 34:22 are the same challenge to call on the false gods; 7:195 is the same challenge. 17:110, in the same surah, tells them to call on God by His names.
tree:0ftuney0pnblw8.relation: Contrast: call on the false gods and see they own nothing; call on God by any of His beautiful names.

tree:11v5dir1cu3mb9.why: The challenge to bring a scripture: the Torah, one surah, ten surahs, a better book. A memorizer must keep the amounts apart.
tree:11v5dir1cu3mb9.relation: The graded challenge to the deniers of the revelation.

tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.why: 9:83 and 48:15 are the same ruling on those who stayed behind: they will not go out with the Prophet. 9:51 and 33:16 are other replies with different subjects.
tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.changes: Removed 9:51 and 33:16: same reply opener, different subjects.
tree:14h6goy0e0aul0.relation: The same answer to the laggards in two campaigns.

tree:0v0mdjg12ep2sa.why: Only the end of one clause and the start of a closing are shared; the subjects (regret of the hypocrites, the mosque of harm, Moses' people) are unrelated.

tree:1i5c7od0b2gtpl.why: Each ayah commands decent, proper speech in a delicate setting: to a woman in her waiting period, to those unable to manage wealth, to relatives at the division of an estate, and by the Prophet's wives to men. 4:5 and 4:8 end the same way, a trap for memorizers.
tree:1i5c7od0b2gtpl.relation: Proper speech as a duty wherever money, marriage or modesty is at stake.

tree:05f7yv50uhb46d.why: 7:109 and 7:127 open the same way in one surah; 26:11 and 44:17 name the same people as the ones Moses was sent to.
tree:05f7yv50uhb46d.relation: Pharaoh's people: their chiefs' accusation and plotting, and God's sending Moses to them as a trial.

tree:189ctge1xbns5m.why: Only a phrase about the prophet's people is shared; the subjects are unrelated (unseen news, Moses' mission, the calf, Noah's mission).

tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.why: Two separate pairs: the chiefs of Noah's people dismissing him as a mere man (11:27, 23:24), and Ibrahim questioning his father and people about their idols (21:52, 26:70). Each pair is a good memorizer set; together they are two different things.
tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.changes: Split into the two pairs that belong together.
tree:0umiy9c1vupsyy.relation: Noah rejected as only a man; Ibrahim's question about what his people worship.

tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.why: 5:106, 6:152 and 35:18 say the same rule: kinship changes nothing, in testimony, in justice, and in bearing another's burden. 68:14 is about a man who has wealth and sons, a different phrase.
tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.changes: Removed 68:14: same words, a different meaning (owning wealth).
tree:0ceo6v11uxxgfd.relation: Kinship never bends testimony, justice or the reckoning.

tree:1nfuua60nst24i.why: 12:38 and 14:11 are believers saying what is not theirs to do; 14:11 and 37:30 both deny having any authority. 3:154 is the hypocrites' wish, a conditional with a different structure.
tree:1nfuua60nst24i.changes: Removed 3:154: its words are a conditional wish, a different structure.
tree:1nfuua60nst24i.relation: What is not ours: to associate partners, to bring a proof without God's leave, to have power over others.

tree:1h47p280pvz9c8.why: Hope in meeting God as the motive for action; 33:21 and 60:6 are near-identical lines about a good example (the Prophet, then Ibrahim), a memorizer trap.
tree:1h47p280pvz9c8.relation: Who hopes for God and the Last Day has a model to follow and deeds to do.

tree:1mu3l7t0je5b43.why: Only a stock closing about what people used to do is shared; the subjects are unrelated (the Children of Israel, sects, Noah's people, the disbelievers' reward).

tree:0yj07el0imtyxt.why: The Quran described as a blessed Book God sent down, each time with a different purpose; 6:92 and 6:155 in one surah open the same way.
tree:0yj07el0imtyxt.relation: The blessed Book: to confirm what came before, to be followed, to bring people to light, to be pondered.

tree:1jd27ea0fmcuuk.why: Thamud's denial, told in four short openings that differ in what they denied; easy to mix up.
tree:1jd27ea0fmcuuk.relation: The same denial seen four ways: the messengers, the warnings, the Hour, out of their arrogance.

tree:115vnec0tc35mw.why: A common phrase for denying the signs, said of unrelated subjects (Pharaoh's people, a warning to the Prophet, the evildoers' end, those given the Torah).

tree:0r12ejn1j7b3a3.why: Each ayah says evil deeds were made to seem fair to someone: the disbelievers, the idolaters killing their children, the wasteful, Pharaoh.
tree:0r12ejn1j7b3a3.relation: How falsehood is made attractive to those who follow it.

tree:0q20doo033nebw.why: 9:54, 9:80 and 9:84 give the same reason for the hypocrites' rejection, with small wording differences a memorizer must catch. 29:52 is a general statement in another context.
tree:0q20doo033nebw.relation: One cause behind three rulings on the hypocrites: their spending refused, no forgiveness, no funeral prayer.

tree:0a4c48017985ms.why: What is said of those who disbelieve in their Lord: they set up equals, they wear chains, their deeds are ashes, they have Hell. The phrase is distinctive and the four continuations are easy to confuse.
tree:0a4c48017985ms.relation: The state and end of those who disbelieve in their Lord.

tree:16pfaou030wjvs.why: 83:7 and 83:18 are a matched pair: the record of the wicked and the record of the righteous. 26:62 (Moses' trust) and 96:6 (man's transgression) share only the particle.
tree:16pfaou030wjvs.changes: Removed 26:62 and 96:6: only the opening particle is shared.
tree:16pfaou030wjvs.relation: Contrast: the record of the wicked in the lowest place and of the righteous in the highest.

tree:0zvdo6o00gcsbi.why: Two separate pairs: the entry into the town by the Children of Israel (2:58, 7:161), a classic memorizer pair, and eating from the sacrificial animals in the Hajj (22:28, 22:36).
tree:0zvdo6o00gcsbi.changes: Split into the two pairs that belong together.

tree:17zwzph19ok6w1.why: Three ayat are excuses or disclaimers of heedlessness, and 23:17 says God is never heedless of His creation.
tree:17zwzph19ok6w1.relation: Contrast: people plead they were heedless, while God is never heedless.

tree:0p4dr9v1wzal8p.why: The question on the Day about the partners they claimed; 28:62 and 28:74 are identical in one surah.
tree:0p4dr9v1wzal8p.relation: The false partners abandon their worshippers on the Day.

tree:0wp41hk09w5t6k.why: A warning form: how will it be when they are gathered, when witnesses are brought, when calamity strikes, when the angels take them.
tree:0wp41hk09w5t6k.relation: Four moments of reckoning, each introduced the same way.

tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.why: 7:188 and 10:49 differ only in the order of harm and benefit, a classic memorizer pair; 72:21 makes the same disclaimer. 5:25 is Moses saying he controls only himself and his brother, a different statement.
tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.changes: Removed 5:25: same verb, a different statement.
tree:0mz33hn13tkilt.relation: The Prophet has no power of benefit or harm except what God wills.

tree:0ksvih017cowf2.why: Two separate things: no fear on the people of Paradise (7:49, 43:68), and the repeated lines of the Kafirun surah (109:3, 109:5).
tree:0ksvih017cowf2.changes: Split into the Paradise pair and the repetition in surah 109.

tree:11jepkl187sdv1.why: Three commands in one passage of al-Isra end with similar threats that a memorizer must keep apart. 59:10 is a prayer about the heart, another subject.
tree:11jepkl187sdv1.changes: Removed 59:10: a prayer, unrelated to the commands of al-Isra.

tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.why: 2:22 and 51:51 both forbid setting up partners with God. 2:224 (oaths) and 24:63 (addressing the Messenger) are different prohibitions.
tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.changes: Removed 2:224 and 24:63: same prohibition form, different subjects.
tree:0tjmepc1kqdx6c.relation: The ban on setting up equals with God, after the signs of creation and after the call to flee to Him.

tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.why: 2:272 and 8:60 promise the same full repayment of what is spent, in almost the same words. 2:279 (usury) and 4:77 (fighting) use the phrase about other things.
tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.changes: Removed 2:279 and 4:77: same closing, different subjects.
tree:1i07ulu189dz1y.relation: Spending in God's cause is repaid in full.

tree:1x2ya9a048o13k.why: No protector or intercessor besides God, said four times with different continuations; a memorizer set and a clear theme.
tree:1x2ya9a048o13k.relation: No one can intercede for a soul except by God's leave.

tree:1cqf67c0ukf4mo.why: All four lift blame from those with a real excuse: the weak, the sick, the poor, the blind and the lame. 24:61 and 48:17 open identically and then go to different subjects (eating in houses, staying from battle), a memorizer trap.
tree:1cqf67c0ukf4mo.relation: Who is excused, and from what: from fighting, and from the rules of eating together.

tree:1ey6zz009o1i8y.why: 6:160, 28:84 and 40:40 state the same justice: an evil deed is repaid only by its like, while good is multiplied. A close memorizer set. 31:33 is about no parent paying for a child, a different statement.
tree:1ey6zz009o1i8y.relation: God's justice and generosity: evil repaid only in kind, good repaid many times.

tree:13x93cp1afczdp.why: Four prohibitions in the rulings on women and marriage: concealing pregnancy, taking back the dower, inheriting women by force, and new marriages for the Prophet.
tree:13x93cp1afczdp.relation: What is not lawful in marriage, for wives, husbands and the Prophet.

tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.why: 20:112 and 72:13 promise the believer the same safety from injustice in matched pairs of words, a memorizer pair (the jinn echo it). 27:10 (the messengers do not fear) and 91:15 (God does not fear the outcome) are different statements.
tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.changes: Removed 27:10 and 91:15: same verb, different subjects.
tree:0oa8zqd040ggg7.relation: The believer fears no wrong: said by God in Taha and by the believing jinn.

tree:1p19bf105qu9yz.why: God never breaks His promise, said four ways; the endings differ (the appointment, His promise) and a memorizer must keep them apart.
tree:1p19bf105qu9yz.relation: Certainty of God's promise: the gathering, the punishment, victory, and Paradise.

tree:0qbzuam1myh73y.why: Each ayah denies that two groups are equal: those who strive and those who sit, the bad and the good, those who spent before the victory and after, the people of the Fire and of Paradise.
tree:0qbzuam1myh73y.relation: The Quran's scale of who is not equal to whom.

tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.why: Who is questioned and who is not: God is not questioned while they are; the criminals are not asked about their sins. 70:10 is a friend not asking after a friend, a different sense.
tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.changes: Removed 70:10: the verb there means asking after someone, not being called to account.
tree:09zhyv41j8cvls.relation: Pondering the questioning: God is beyond question, and on that Day the guilty are known without being asked.

tree:00ehd0c0pmjkvo.why: The enemies of the believers will not be helped: 3:111 and 59:12 end the same way about turning their backs; 28:41 and 41:16 say it of Pharaoh's people and of Ad in the Hereafter.
tree:00ehd0c0pmjkvo.relation: Those who fight God's people end without help, here and in the Hereafter.

tree:0p3z5lq0g8y2wy.why: Ibrahim confronting his father and people, four times with different wording; a classic memorizer set.
tree:0p3z5lq0g8y2wy.relation: Ibrahim's challenge to idol worship, from questioning to disowning.

tree:0awe2fv1i40219.why: God's oath to fill Hell, said to Iblis (7:18, 38:85) and as His decreed word (11:119, 32:13); the endings differ in ways a memorizer must hold.
tree:0awe2fv1i40219.relation: The decree that Hell will be filled, from Iblis' followers among jinn and men.

tree:0oinr331gcwm9p.why: The descent of Adam with enmity between them, told three times with different continuations; 43:67 turns the same words to friends who become enemies on the Day.
tree:0oinr331gcwm9p.relation: Enmity on earth since the fall, and the friends who turn enemies on the Day except the God-fearing.

tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.why: 2:131, 6:71 and 40:66 are about submitting to the Lord of the worlds: Ibrahim's answer and the Prophet's command. 83:6 is people standing before Him on the Day, a different statement.
tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.changes: Removed 83:6 (with 83:7): same name of God, different subject.
tree:0t2dwiy1dyueh6.relation: Submission to the Lord of the worlds, by Ibrahim and by the Prophet.

tree:13a2m461scp1a2.why: God telling that He sent down clear signs, with different continuations; 24:34 and 24:46 in one surah are a memorizer trap.
tree:13a2m461scp1a2.relation: Clear revelation, and who benefits from it and who rejects it.

tree:0po3g9u11vm86k.why: The proof had already reached them: a messenger, Moses, guidance, warning news. Each time the people turned away anyway.
tree:0po3g9u11vm86k.relation: No excuse remains: guidance came, and was rejected.

tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.why: 11:79, 17:102 and 21:65 have one side tell the other you know well; in 17:102 and 21:65 the opponent is made to admit a truth he knows. 37:158 is about what the jinn know, a different sentence.
tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.changes: Removed 37:158: the jinn as subject, a different sentence.
tree:1s2rnwe05vgg30.relation: The truth the opponent already knows: Pharaoh knows who sent the signs, Ibrahim's people know idols cannot speak.

tree:10xz6bu1u4h8uo.why: A stock closing about people of certainty, after unrelated subjects (demands for a sign, judgement, creation, the Quran as insight).

tree:0ijz7qe1r23eba.why: 2:54, 5:20 and 61:5 are Moses addressing his people with the same opening and different messages: repent of the calf, remember God's favour, why do you hurt me. 10:71 is Noah, another story.
tree:0ijz7qe1r23eba.relation: Moses and his people: rebuke, reminder and complaint.

tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.why: 6:154, 7:145 and 16:89 describe a scripture that explains everything: the Torah twice and the Quran. 65:3 is God setting a measure for everything, a different phrase.
tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.changes: Removed 65:3: same words, a different meaning (a measure).
tree:0wl7y3m0bmtmjc.relation: The Torah and the Quran each given as a full explanation, guidance and mercy.

tree:1e11yto0taka30.why: 2:139, 28:55 and 42:15 use the same line of separation, each with a different ending. 33:71 is God setting your deeds right, a different phrase.
tree:1e11yto0taka30.changes: Removed 33:71: same words, different structure and meaning.
tree:1e11yto0taka30.relation: Parting with opponents without quarrel: we have our deeds and you yours.

tree:03e2w031w2oofl.why: Two unrelated subjects meet only on a short phrase: speaking without knowledge, and rain bringing out crops. The real pairs are kept elsewhere.

tree:15n3grz19nd0b7.why: 37:154 and 68:36 are the same rebuke, and 10:35 has it with a different opening. 14:45 is about what became clear to them, a different structure.
tree:15n3grz19nd0b7.relation: The rebuke to those who judge wrongly about God.

tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.why: 11:2, 51:50 and 51:51 are the Prophet's declaration that he is a warner from God; 51:50 and 51:51 repeat it back to back. 16:10 is water to drink, a different meaning.
tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.changes: Removed 16:10 and made the three warner ayat one row each (the old rows repeated 51:51).
tree:1jhwx9u0yymjay.relation: The messenger as a clear warner from God.

tree:1ahlfyq03q4clq.why: The reward of those who do good; 16:30 and 39:10 share the same clause, a memorizer pair.
tree:1ahlfyq03q4clq.relation: Good done is repaid with good, in this world and more in the next.

tree:1ejedju0oiehk8.why: The weak blaming the arrogant leaders on the Day; 14:21 and 40:47 open identically.
tree:1ejedju0oiehk8.relation: Followers and leaders turn on each other when they face the punishment.

tree:12apeh01iaxsy4.why: The same threat with small changes a memorizer must hold apart: the verb of preparing and the kind of punishment. 4:37 and 4:151 are identical in one surah.
